If "man" is understood generally, the meaning is that they will kneel when they reach the shore of Hell. And "jithiyyan" is a circumstantial state that is anticipated, since they were in the place of standing kneeling, for that is part of the standing for reckoning, before arriving at reward and punishment.

It is said that the meaning of "We shall surely bring them forth around Hell, kneeling" (jithiyyan) is kneeling on their knees, according to Mujahid and Qatada, meaning that because of the severity of their condition they are unable to stand. "Around Hell" (hawla jahannam) may mean within it, as one says: "The people sat around the house," meaning inside it, surrounding it. So the phrase "around Hell" on this interpretation may be after entering, and it may be before entering.

"Jithiyy" is the plural of "jathin." It is said: "jatha 'ala rukbatayhi, yajthu wa yajthi juthuwwan wa juthiyyan," on the pattern fu'ul in both forms. "Ajthahu ghayruhu" means another made him kneel. A people may be called "juthiyy" as in "jalasa juluusan" (he sat), and the people are "juluus" and "jithiyy," also with a kasra on the jim because of the kasra after it. Ibn Abbas said: "jithiyyan" means in groups. Muqatil said: "jam'an jam'an" (in gatherings). On this interpretation, it is the plural of "juthwa," "jathwa" and "jithwa," three dialectal forms, meaning gathered stones and gathered earth. Thus the people of wine are apart, and the people of fornication are apart. Likewise Tarafa said:

"You see two mounds of earth upon them,
Hard slabs of closely laid stone upon them."

Al-Hasan and al-Dahhak said: "jathiyatan" means kneeling on the knees. On this interpretation it is the plural of "jathin," as explained earlier. This is because of the narrowness of the place, meaning that they cannot sit fully. It was also said: "jithiyyan" means kneeling on their knees for disputing, as in the saying of Allah: "Then on the Day of Resurrection, before your Lord, you will dispute" [al-Zumar: 31] [See vol. 15, p. 254.]. Al-Kumayt said:

"They left their nobles kneeling,
While they, beneath the nobles, were bound together."

The saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Then We shall surely draw out from every sect﴾, that is, We shall extract from every community and every religious group ("ayyuhum ashaddu 'ala al-Rahman 'itiyya") whichever of them is most defiant against the Most Merciful.

Al-Nahhas said: This is a verse difficult in its grammatical analysis (i'rab), because all the readers recite "ayyuhum" with a nominative ending except Harun the Blind reader, for Sibawayh related from him: "Thumma lananzi'anna min kulli shi'atin ayyahum" with the accusative, governed by "lananzi'anna" (we shall surely draw out). Abu Ishaq said: there are three opinions concerning the nominative of "ayyuhum." Al-Khalil ibn Ahmad said, as related from him by Sibawayh, that it is nominative by way of quotation, the meaning being: "Then We shall surely draw out from every sect the one who is said, because of his defiance: which of them is most defiant against the Most Merciful." Al-Khalil recited:

"I have spent nights with a girl in a place,
So I spent the night neither troubled nor deprived."

That is, I spent the night in the position of one of whom it is said: "He is neither troubled nor deprived." Abu Ja'far al-Nahhas said: I saw Abu Ishaq choose this opinion and approve of it. He said: because it is the meaning of the statement of the people of tafsir. He also claimed that the meaning of "Then We shall surely draw out from every sect" is: then We shall surely draw out from every group the most defiant, then the next most defiant. It is as if the torment begins with the most defiant among them, then the one after him. This is the exact wording of Abu Ishaq regarding the meaning of the verse.

Yunus said: "lananzi'anna" has the status of verbs that are cancelled (in their governing), and "ayyuhum" is nominative as the subject. Al-Mahdawi said: the verb is "lananzi'anna," and according to Yunus it is suspended (mu'allaq). Abu Ali said: the meaning of that is that it governs the position of "ayyuhum ashaddu," not that it is cancelled. Al-Khalil and Sibawayh do not suspend a verb like "lananzi'anna" with such a construction; suspension applies only to verbs of doubt and what resembles them, when the occurrence is not certain.

Sibawayh said: "ayyuhum" is built on damma, because it differs from its sisters in the matter of omission. For if you say "ra'aytu alladhi afdalu" (I saw the one who is more excellent) or "man afdalu" (who is more excellent), it is ugly, until you say "man huwa afdalu" (who is he who is more excellent). The omission in "ayyihim" is permissible. Abu Ja'far said: I do not know of any grammarian who has not criticized Sibawayh on this point. I heard Abu Ishaq say: it does not appear clear to me that Sibawayh erred in his book except in two places, and this is one of them. He said: We know that Sibawayh parsed "ayy" as declinable, since it is put in construct, so how can he make it indeclinable when it is in construct? Abu Ishaq did not mention, as far as I know, anything beyond these three opinions. Abu Ali said: the construction on the school of Sibawayh is necessary, because he omitted from it what makes it definite, namely the pronoun, while needing it, just as it is omitted in "min qablu wa min ba'du" [al-Rum: 4] (the two words by which they are defined), in that the attributive clause (silah) clarifies and explains the relative pronoun, just as the second noun in construct clarifies and specifies the first.

Abu Ja'far said: there are four other opinions besides these three mentioned by Abu Ishaq. Al-Kisa'i said: "lananzi'anna" governs the meaning, as one says: "I wore some of the garments and I ate some of the food," and "lananzi'anna" does not govern "ayyuhum" so as to put it in the accusative. Al-Mahdawi added: the verb according to him governs the place of "min kulli shi'atin," and the statement "ayyuhum ashaddu" is a new sentence, nominative as the subject. Sibawayh does not hold that "min" is added in an affirmative sentence. Al-Farra' said: the meaning is "thumma lananzi'anna" by calling (bi-al-nida'), and the meaning of "lananzi'anna" is "lananadiyanna" (we shall surely call out). Al-Mahdawi said: "nada" is a verb that is suspended when followed by a sentence, like "zanantu" (I thought), so it governs in meaning but does not govern in wording. Abu Ja'far said: Abu Bakr ibn Shuqayr related that some of the Kufans say concerning "ayyuhum" that it has the meaning of a condition and conditional consequence, and therefore what precedes it does not govern it. The meaning is: "Then We shall surely draw out from every sect, whether they follow one another or do not follow one another," just as you say: "I struck the people, whichever of them became angry," meaning whether they became angry or did not become angry.

Abu Ja'far said: these are six opinions. I heard Ali ibn Sulayman relate from Muhammad ibn Yazid that he said: "ayyuhum" is connected to "shi'atin" (sect), so it is nominative as the subject, and the meaning is: "Then We shall surely draw out from those who followed one another whichever of them" (ayyuhum), that is, from those who cooperated, so they look at which of them is most defiant against the Most Merciful. This is a good opinion. Al-Kisa'i related that "tashaya'a" means cooperation. "'Itiyyan" is in the accusative as clarification (tamyiz).

The saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Then indeed We are most knowing of those who most deserve to be burned therein﴾ (verse 70). [In the margin: "(Sallyan)" with a damma on the sad is the reading of Nafi', and the exegesis is based on it.] That is, most deserving of entering the Fire. It is said: "salla yasla sulliyyan," like "madha al-shay'u yamdi mudiyyan" (the thing passed away) when it departs, and "hawa yahwi huwiyyan" (he fell) . Al-Jawhari said: it is said: "salayt al-rajul naran" when you make the man enter the Fire and make him burn in it. If you cast him into it with force, as though you intend burning, you say: "asleytuhu" with alif, and "salayatuhu tasliyatan." Those who read it with a light ending say: from the expression: "salya fulan bi-al-nar" (with kasra), "yasla sillyyan," meaning he was burned. Allah, the Exalted, said: "they are most deserving of it, burning" (ṣilyyan). Al-Ajjaj said:

"By Allah, were it not for the Fire that we would burn in it,
Or the people invoking Allah against us,
We would not have heard the obedience of the commander."

[He is ascribed in Lisan al-Arab, under the root (fih), to al-Zafayan, and he cited it in verses which are:
"What is the matter with an eye that wept for its longing,
Over the traces of a dwelling worn by its decay?
By Allah, were it not for the Fire that we would burn in it,
Or the people invoking Allah against us,
We would not have heard the obedience of the commander."
"Alqahu": obedience.]

It is also said: "saliya bi-al-amr" when he endured its heat and severity. Al-Tuhawi said:

[The verse of al-Tuhawi is not completed in the text.]

بَسَالَتُهُمْ وَإِنْ هُمْ ... صَلُوا بِالْحَرْبِ حِينًا بَعْدَ حِينٍ
وَاصْطَلَيْتُ بِالنَّارِ وَتَصَلَّيْتُ بِهَا. قَالَ أَبُو زُبَيْدٍ:
وَقَدْ تَصَلَّيْتُ حَرَّ حَرْبِهِمْ ... كَمَا تَصَلَّى الْمَقْرُورُ مِنْ قَرَسٍ
وَفُلَانٌ لَا يُصْطَلَى بِنَارِهِ إِذَا كَانَ شُجَاعًا لَا يُطَاقُ.

قَوْلُهُ تَعَالَى: ﴿وَإِنْ مِنْكُمْ إِلَّا وارِدُها كانَ عَلى رَبِّكَ حَتْماً مَقْضِيًّا﴾ فِيهِ خَمْسُ مَسَائِلَ:

الْأُولَى: قَوْلُهُ تَعَالَى: ﴿وَإِنْ مِنْكُمْ﴾ هَذَا قَسَمٌ وَالْوَاوُ يَتَضَمَّنُهُ. وَيُفَسِّرُهُ حَدِيثُ النَّبِيِّ (ﷺ): (لَا يَمُوتُ لِأَحَدٍ مِنَ الْمُسْلِمِينَ ثَلَاثَةٌ مِنَ الْوَلَدِ فَتَمَسُّهُ النَّارُ إِلَّا تَحِلَّةَ الْقَسَمِ).
([إِلَّا تَحِلَّةَ الْقَسَمِ]: أَيْ لَا يَدْخُلُ النَّارَ لِيُعَاقَبَ بِهَا، وَلَكِنَّهُ يَجُوزُ عَلَيْهَا، فَلَا يَكُونُ ذَلِكَ إِلَّا بِقَدْرِ مَا يُبِرُّ اللَّهُ بِهِ قَسَمَهُ.)
قَالَ الزُّهْرِيُّ: كَأَنَّهُ يُرِيدُ هَذِهِ الْآيَةَ ﴿وَإِنْ مِنْكُمْ إِلَّا وارِدُها﴾. ذَكَرَهُ أَبُو دَاوُدَ الطَّيَالِسِيُّ. فَقَوْلُهُ: "إِلَّا تَحِلَّةَ الْقَسَمِ" يُخَرَّجُ فِي التَّفْسِيرِ الْمُسْنَدِ، لِأَنَّ الْقَسَمَ الْمَذْكُورَ فِي هَذَا الْحَدِيثِ مَعْنَاهُ عِنْدَ أَهْلِ الْعِلْمِ قَوْلُهُ تَعَالَى: ﴿وَإِنْ مِنْكُمْ إِلَّا وارِدُها﴾. وَقَدْ قِيلَ إِنَّ الْمُرَادَ بِالْقَسَمِ قَوْلُهُ تَعَالَى: ﴿وَالذَّارِياتِ ذَرْواً﴾ إِلَى قَوْلِهِ: ﴿إِنَّما تُوعَدُونَ لَصادِقٌ. وَإِنَّ الدِّينَ لَواقِعٌ﴾ [راجع ج ١٧ ص ٢٩]. وَالْأَوَّلُ أَشْهَرُ، وَالْمَعْنَى مُتَقَارِبٌ.

الثَّانِيَةُ: اخْتَلَفَ النَّاسُ فِي الْوُرُودِ، فَقِيلَ: الْوُرُودُ الدُّخُولُ. رُوِيَ عَنْ جَابِرِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ قَالَ: سَمِعْتُ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ (ﷺ) يَقُولُ: (الْوُرُودُ الدُّخُولُ، لَا يَبْقَى بَرٌّ وَلَا فَاجِرٌ إِلَّا دَخَلَهَا، فَتَكُونُ عَلَى الْمُؤْمِنِينَ بَرْدًا وَسَلَامًا كَمَا كَانَتْ عَلَى إِبْرَاهِيمَ). ﴿ثُمَّ نُنَجِّي الَّذِينَ اتَّقَوْا وَنَذَرُ الظَّالِمِينَ فِيها جِثِيًّا﴾. أَسْنَدَهُ أَبُو عُمَرَ فِي كِتَابِ "التَّمْهِيدِ". وَهُوَ قَوْلُ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ وَخَالِدِ بْنِ مَعْدَانَ وَابْنِ جُرَيْجٍ وَغَيْرِهِمْ.

وَرُوِيَ عَنْ يُونُسَ [عَنِ الْحُسَيْنِ] أَنَّهُ كَانَ يَقْرَأُ: ﴿وَإِنْ مِنْكُمْ إِلَّا وارِدُها﴾ "الْوُرُودُ الدُّخُولُ" عَلَى التَّفْسِيرِ لِلْوُرُودِ، فَغَلِطَ فِيهِ بَعْضُ الرُّوَاةِ فَأَلْحَقَهُ بِالْقُرْآنِ.

وَفِي مُسْنَدِ الدَّارِمِيِّ عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ مَسْعُودٍ قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ (ﷺ): (يَرِدُ النَّاسُ النَّارَ ثُمَّ يَصْدُرُونَ مِنْهَا بِأَعْمَالِهِمْ، فَأَوَّلُهُمْ كَلَمْحِ الْبَرْقِ، ثُمَّ كَالرِّيحِ، ثُمَّ كَحُضْرِ الْفَرَسِ، ثُمَّ كَالرَّاكِبِ الْمُجِدِّ فِي رَحْلِهِ، ثُمَّ كَشَدِّ الرَّجُلِ فِي مِشْيَتِهِ).
[الْحُضْرُ (بِالضَّمِّ): الْعَدْوُ، وَشَدُّ الرَّجُلِ: عَدْوُهُ أَيْضًا.]

وَرُوِيَ عَنِ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ أَنَّهُ قَالَ فِي هَذِهِ الْمَسْأَلَةِ لِنَافِعِ بْنِ الْأَزْرَقِ الْخَارِجِيِّ: أَمَّا أَنَا وَأَنْتَ فَلَا بُدَّ أَنْ نَرِدَهَا؛ أَمَّا أَنَا فَيُنْجِينِي اللَّهُ مِنْهَا، وَأَمَّا أَنْتَ فَمَا أَظُنُّهُ يُنْجِيكَ لِتَكْذِيبِكَ.

وَقَدْ أَشْفَقَ كَثِيرٌ مِنَ الْعُلَمَاءِ مِنْ تَحَقُّقِ الْوُرُودِ وَالْجَهْلِ بِالصَّدْرِ، وَقَدْ بَيَّنَّاهُ فِي "التَّذْكِرَةِ".

وَقَالَتْ فِرْقَةٌ: الْوُرُودُ الْمَمَرُّ عَلَى الصِّرَاطِ. وَرُوِيَ ذَلِكَ عَنِ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ وَابْنِ مَسْعُودٍ وَكَعْبِ الْأَحْبَارِ وَالسُّدِّيِّ، وَرَوَاهُ السُّدِّيُّ عَنِ ابْنِ مَسْعُودٍ عَنِ النَّبِيِّ (ﷺ). وَقَالَهُ الْحَسَنُ أَيْضًا، قَالَ: لَيْسَ الْوُرُودُ الدُّخُولَ، إِنَّمَا تَقُولُ: وَرَدْتُ الْبَصْرَةَ وَلَمْ أَدْخُلْهَا. قَالَ: فَالْوُرُودُ أَنْ يَمُرُّوا عَلَى الصِّرَاطِ.

قَالَ أَبُو بَكْرٍ الْأَنْبَارِيُّ: وَقَدْ بَنَى عَلَى مَذْهَبِ الْحَسَنِ قَوْمٌ مِنْ أَهْلِ اللُّغَةِ، وَاحْتَجُّوا بِقَوْلِ اللَّهِ تَعَالَى: ﴿إِنَّ الَّذِينَ سَبَقَتْ لَهُمْ مِنَّا الْحُسْنى أُولئِكَ عَنْها مُبْعَدُونَ﴾ [راجع ص ٣٤٥ مِنْ هَذَا الْجُزْءِ]. قَالُوا: فَلَا يَدْخُلُ النَّارَ مَنْ ضَمِنَ اللَّهُ أَنْ يُبْعِدَهُ مِنْهَا. وَكَانَ هَؤُلَاءِ يَقْرَءُونَ "ثَمَّ" بِفَتْحِ الثَّاءِ: ﴿ثَمَّ نُنَجِّي الَّذِينَ اتَّقَوْا﴾.

وَاحْتَجَّ عَلَيْهِمُ الْآخَرُونَ، أَهْلُ الْمَقَالَةِ الْأُولَى، بِأَنَّ مَعْنَى قَوْلِهِ: ﴿أُولئِكَ عَنْها مُبْعَدُونَ﴾ عَنِ الْعَذَابِ فِيهَا وَالْإِحْرَاقِ بِهَا. قَالُوا: فَمَنْ دَخَلَهَا وَهُوَ لَا يَشْعُرُ بِهَا وَلَا يُحِسُّ مِنْهَا وَجَعًا وَلَا أَلَمًا، فَهُوَ مُبْعَدٌ عَنْهَا فِي الْحَقِيقَةِ. وَيَسْتَدِلُّونَ بِقَوْلِهِ تَعَالَى: ﴿ثُمَّ نُنَجِّي الَّذِينَ اتَّقَوْا﴾ بِضَمِّ الثَّاءِ، فَ"ثُمَّ" تَدُلُّ عَلَى نَجَاءٍ بَعْدَ الدُّخُولِ.

قُلْتُ: وَفِي صَحِيحِ مُسْلِمٍ: (ثُمَّ يُضْرَبُ الْجِسْرُ عَلَى جَهَنَّمَ، وَتَحِلُّ الشَّفَاعَةُ، فَيَقُولُونَ: اللَّهُمَّ سَلِّمْ سَلِّمْ). قِيلَ: يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ وَمَا الْجِسْرُ؟ قَالَ: (دَحْضٌ مَزِلَّةٌ [دَحْضٌ مَزِلَّةٌ: هُمَا بِمَعْنًى، وَهُوَ الْمَوْضِعُ الَّذِي تَنْزِلُ فِيهِ الْأَقْدَامُ وَلَا تَسْتَقِرُّ] فِيهِ خَطَاطِيفُ وَكَلَالِيبُ وَحَسَكٌ، تَكُونُ بِنَجْدٍ، فِيهَا شُوَيْكَةٌ يُقَالُ لَهَا السَّعْدَانُ، فَيَمُرُّ الْمُؤْمِنُونَ كَطَرْفِ الْعَيْنِ، وَكَالْبَرْقِ، وَكَالرِّيحِ، وَكَالطَّيْرِ، وَكَأَجَاوِيدِ الْخَيْلِ وَالرِّكَابِ، فَنَاجٍ مُسَلَّمٌ، وَمَخْدُوشٌ مُرْسَلٌ، وَمَكْدُوسٌ فِي نَارِ جَهَنَّمَ) الْحَدِيثَ.

وَبِهِ احْتَجَّ مَنْ قَالَ: إِنَّ الْجَوَازَ عَلَى الصِّرَاطِ هُوَ الْوُرُودُ الَّذِي تَضَمَّنَتْهُ هَذِهِ الْآيَةُ، لَا الدُّخُولُ فِيهَا.

وَقَالَتْ فِرْقَةٌ: بَلْ هُوَ وُرُودُ إِشْرَافٍ وَاطِّلَاعٍ وَقُرْبٍ، وَذَلِكَ أَنَّهُمْ يَحْضُرُونَ مَوْضِعَ الْحِسَابِ، وَهُوَ بِقُرْبِ جَهَنَّمَ، فَيَرَوْنَهَا وَيَنْظُرُونَ إِلَيْهَا فِي حَالَةِ الْحِسَابِ، ثُمَّ يُنَجِّي اللَّهُ الَّذِينَ اتَّقَوْا مِمَّا نَظَرُوا إِلَيْهِ وَيُصَارُ بِهِمْ إِلَى الْجَنَّةِ، ﴿وَنَذَرُ الظَّالِمِينَ﴾ أَيْ يُؤْمَرُ بِهِمْ إِلَى النَّارِ. قَالَ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى: ﴿وَلَمَّا وَرَدَ ماءَ مَدْيَنَ﴾ [راجع ج ١٣ ص ٢٦٧] أَيْ أَشْرَفَ عَلَيْهِ، لَا أَنَّهُ دَخَلَهُ. وَقَالَ زُهَيْرٌ:
فَلَمَّا وَرَدْنَ الْمَاءَ زُرْقًا [يُقَالُ: مَاءٌ أَزْرَقُ إِذَا كَانَ صَافِيًا. وَجِمَامُهُ: جَمْعُ جَمٍّ، وَهُوَ الْمَاءُ الْمُجْتَمِعُ. وَالْحَاضِرُ: النَّازِلُ عَلَى الْمَاءِ. وَالْمُتَخَيِّمُ: الْمُقِيمُ، وَأَصْلُهُ مِنْ تَخَيَّمَ إِذَا نَصَبَ الْخَيْمَةَ. يَصِفُ زُهَيْرٌ الظَّعَائِنَ بِأَنَّهُنَّ فِي أَمْنٍ وَمَنَعَةٍ، فَإِذَا نَزَلْنَ نَزَلْنَ آمِنَاتٍ كَنُزُولِ مَنْ هُوَ فِي أَهْلِهِ وَوَطَنِهِ. وَالْبَيْتُ مِنْ مُعَلَّقَتِهِ.]
جِمَامُهُ ... وَضَعْنَ عِصِيَّ الْحَاضِرِ الْمُتَخَيِّمِ

وَرَوَتْ حَفْصَةُ أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ (ﷺ) قَالَ: (لَا يَدْخُلُ النَّارَ أَحَدٌ مِنْ أَهْلِ بَدْرٍ وَالْحُدَيْبِيَةِ). قَالَتْ: فَقُلْتُ: يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ، وَأَيْنَ قَوْلُ اللَّهِ تَعَالَى: ﴿وَإِنْ مِنْكُمْ إِلَّا وارِدُها﴾؟ فَقَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ (ﷺ): (فَمَهْ! ﴿ثُمَّ نُنَجِّي الَّذِينَ اتَّقَوْا وَنَذَرُ الظَّالِمِينَ فِيها جِثِيًّا﴾). أَخْرَجَهُ مُسْلِمٌ مِنْ حَدِيثِ أُمِّ مُبَشِّرٍ، قَالَتْ: سَمِعْتُ النَّبِيَّ (ﷺ) يَقُولُ عِنْدَ حَفْصَةَ الْحَدِيثَ.

وَرَجَّحَ الزَّجَّاجُ هَذَا الْقَوْلَ بِقَوْلِهِ تَعَالَى: ﴿إِنَّ الَّذِينَ سَبَقَتْ لَهُمْ مِنَّا الْحُسْنى أُولئِكَ عَنْها مُبْعَدُونَ﴾.

وَقَالَ مُجَاهِدٌ: وُرُودُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ النَّارَ هُوَ الْحُمَّى الَّتِي تُصِيبُ الْمُؤْمِنَ فِي دَارِ الدُّنْيَا، وَهِيَ حَظُّ الْمُؤْمِنِ مِنَ النَّارِ، فَلَا يَرِدُهَا. وَرَوَى أَبُو هُرَيْرَةَ أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ (ﷺ) عَادَ مَرِيضًا مِنْ وَعْكٍ بِهِ، فَقَالَ لَهُ النَّبِيُّ (ﷺ): (أَبْشِرْ، فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ تَبَارَكَ وَتَعَالَى يَقُولُ: "هِيَ نَارِي أُسَلِّطُهَا عَلَى عَبْدِيَ الْمُؤْمِنِ لِتَكُونَ حَظَّهُ مِنَ النَّارِ").

[أَسْنَدَهُ أَبُو عُمَرَ قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا عَبْدُ الْوَارِثِ بْنُ سُفْيَانَ قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا قَاسِمُ بْنُ أَصْبَغَ قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ إِسْمَاعِيلَ الصَّائِغُ قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا أَبُو أُسَامَةَ قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنُ يَزِيدَ بْنِ جَابِرٍ عَنْ إِسْمَاعِيلَ بْنِ عُبَيْدِ اللَّهِ [عَنْ أَبِي صَالِحٍ الْأَشْعَرِيِّ] عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ عَنِ النَّبِيِّ (ﷺ) عَادَ مَرِيضًا فَذَكَرَهُ.] [الزِّيَادَةُ مِنْ (تَهْذِيبِ التَّهْذِيبِ) وَتَفْسِيرِ الطَّبَرِيِّ.]

وَفِي الْحَدِيثِ: (الْحُمَّى حَظُّ الْمُؤْمِنِ مِنَ النَّارِ).

وَقَالَتْ فِرْقَةٌ: الْوُرُودُ النَّظَرُ إِلَيْهَا فِي الْقَبْرِ، فَيُنَجَّى مِنْهَا الْفَائِزُ، وَيَصْلَاهَا مَنْ قُدِّرَ عَلَيْهِ دُخُولُهَا، ثُمَّ يَخْرُجُ مِنْهَا بِالشَّفَاعَةِ أَوْ بِغَيْرِهَا مِنْ رَحْمَةِ اللَّهِ تَعَالَى. وَاحْتَجُّوا بِحَدِيثِ ابْنِ عُمَرَ: (إِذَا مَاتَ أَحَدُكُمْ عُرِضَ عَلَيْهِ مَقْعَدُهُ بِالْغَدَاةِ وَالْعَشِيِّ) الْحَدِيثَ.

وَرَوَى وَكِيعٌ عَنْ شُعْبَةَ عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ السَّائِبِ عَنْ رَجُلٍ عَنِ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ أَنَّهُ قَالَ فِي قَوْلِ اللَّهِ تَعَالَى: ﴿وَإِنْ مِنْكُمْ إِلَّا وارِدُها﴾ قَالَ: هَذَا خِطَابٌ لِلْكُفَّارِ. وَرُوِيَ عَنْهُ أَنَّهُ كَانَ يَقْرَأُ: ﴿وَإِنْ مِنْهُمْ﴾ رَدًّا عَلَى الْآيَاتِ الَّتِي قَبْلَهَا فِي الْكُفَّارِ، وَهِيَ قَوْلُهُ: ﴿فَوَ رَبِّكَ لَنَحْشُرَنَّهُمْ وَالشَّياطِينَ ثُمَّ لَنُحْضِرَنَّهُمْ حَوْلَ جَهَنَّمَ جِثِيًّا. ثُمَّ لَنَنْزِعَنَّ مِنْ كُلِّ شِيعَةٍ أَيُّهُمْ أَشَدُّ عَلَى الرَّحْمنِ عِتِيًّا. ثُمَّ لَنَحْنُ أَعْلَمُ بِالَّذِينَ هُمْ أَوْلى بِها صِلِيًّا﴾ [مريم: ٦٨ - ٧٠]. وَ﴿وَإِنْ مِنْهُمْ﴾ [مريم: ٧١]. وَكَذَلِكَ قَرَأَ عِكْرِمَةُ وَجَمَاعَةٌ، وَعَلَيْهَا فَلَا شَغَبَ [كَذَا فِي (ب) وَ(ج) وَ(ك) بِالْمُعْجَمَةِ، وَفِي (ا) وَ(ز) وَ(ط) بِالْمُهْمَلَةِ] فِي هَذِهِ الْقِرَاءَةِ.

وَقَالَتْ فِرْقَةٌ: الْمُرَادُ بِ(مِنْكُمْ) الْكَفَرَةُ، وَالْمَعْنَى: قُلْ لَهُمْ يَا مُحَمَّدُ. وَهَذَا التَّأْوِيلُ أَيْضًا سَهْلُ التَّنَاوُلِ، وَالْكَافُ فِي (مِنْكُمْ) رَاجِعَةٌ إِلَى الْهَاءِ فِي (لَنَحْشُرَنَّهُمْ وَالشَّياطِينَ. ثُمَّ لَنُحْضِرَنَّهُمْ حَوْلَ جَهَنَّمَ جِثِيًّا)، فَلَا يُنْكَرُ رُجُوعُ الْكَافِ إِلَى الْهَاءِ، فَقَدْ عُرِفَ ذَلِكَ فِي قَوْلِهِ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ: ﴿وَسَقاهُمْ رَبُّهُمْ شَراباً طَهُوراً. إِنَّ هَذا كانَ لَكُمْ جَزاءً وَكانَ سَعْيُكُمْ مَشْكُوراً﴾ [الإنسان: ٢١ - ٢٢] [راجع ج ١٩ ص ١٤١ فما بعد]، مَعْنَاهُ: كَانَ لَهُمْ، فَرَجَعَتِ الْكَافُ إِلَى الْهَاءِ.

وَقَالَ الْأَكْثَرُ: الْمُخَاطَبُ الْعَالَمُ كُلُّهُ، وَلَا بُدَّ مِنْ وُرُودِ الْجَمِيعِ، وَعَلَيْهِ نَشَأَ الْخِلَافُ فِي الْوُرُودِ، وَقَدْ بَيَّنَّا أَقْوَالَ الْعُلَمَاءِ فِيهِ. وَظَاهِرُ الْوُرُودِ الدُّخُولُ لِقَوْلِهِ عَلَيْهِ الصَّلَاةُ وَالسَّلَامُ: (فَتَمَسُّهُ النَّارُ)، لِأَنَّ الْمَسَّ حَقِيقَتُهُ فِي اللُّغَةِ الْمُمَاسَّةُ، إِلَّا أَنَّهَا تَكُونُ بَرْدًا وَسَلَامًا عَلَى الْمُؤْمِنِينَ، وَيَنْجُونَ مِنْهَا سَالِمِينَ.

قَالَ خَالِدُ بْنُ مَعْدَانَ: إِذَا دَخَلَ أَهْلُ الْجَنَّةِ الْجَنَّةَ قَالُوا: أَلَمْ يَقُلْ رَبُّنَا: ﴿إِنَّا نَرِدُ النَّارَ﴾؟ فَيُقَالُ: لَقَدْ وَرَدْتُمُوهَا فَأُلْقِيَتْ رَمَادًا.

قُلْتُ: وَهَذَا الْقَوْلُ يَجْمَعُ شَتَاتَ الْأَقْوَالِ، فَإِنَّ مَنْ وَرَدَهَا وَلَمْ تُؤْذِهِ بِلَهَبِهَا وَحَرِّهَا فَقَدْ أُبْعِدَ عَنْهَا وَنُجِّيَ مِنْهَا. نَجَّانَا اللَّهُ تَعَالَى مِنْهَا بِفَضْلِهِ وَكَرَمِهِ، وَجَعَلَنَا مِمَّنْ وَرَدَهَا فَدَخَلَهَا سَالِمًا وَخَرَجَ مِنْهَا غَانِمًا.

فَإِنْ قِيلَ: فَهَلْ يَدْخُلُ الْأَنْبِيَاءُ النَّارَ؟ قُلْنَا: لَا نُطْلِقُ هَذَا، وَلَكِنْ نَقُولُ: إِنَّ الْخَلْقَ جَمِيعًا يَرِدُونَهَا كَمَا دَلَّ عَلَيْهِ حَدِيثُ جَابِرٍ أَوَّلَ الْبَابِ، فَالْعُصَاةُ يَدْخُلُونَهَا بِجَرَائِمِهِمْ، وَالْأَوْلِيَاءُ وَالسُّعَدَاءُ لِشَفَاعَتِهِمْ، فَبَيْنَ الدُّخُولَيْنِ بَوْنٌ.

وَقَالَ ابْنُ الْأَنْبَارِيِّ مُحْتَجًّا لِمُصْحَفِ عُثْمَانَ وَقِرَاءَةِ الْعَامَّةِ: جَائِزٌ فِي اللُّغَةِ أَنْ يُرْجَعَ مِنْ خِطَابِ الْغَيْبَةِ إِلَى لَفْظِ الْمُوَاجَهَةِ بِالْخِطَابِ، كَمَا قَالَ: ﴿وَسَقاهُمْ رَبُّهُمْ شَراباً طَهُوراً. إِنَّ هَذا كانَ لَكُمْ جَزاءً وَكانَ سَعْيُكُمْ مَشْكُوراً﴾، فَأَبْدَلَ الْكَافَ مِنَ الْهَاءِ. وَقَدْ تَقَدَّمَ هَذَا الْمَعْنَى فِي (يُونُسَ) [راجع ج ٨ ص ٣٢٤ فما بعد].

الثَّالِثَةُ: الِاسْتِثْنَاءُ فِي قَوْلِهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ: (إِلَّا تَحِلَّةَ الْقَسَمِ) يَحْتَمِلُ أَنْ يَكُونَ اسْتِثْنَاءً مُنْقَطِعًا: لَكِنْ تَحِلَّةُ الْقَسَمِ، وَهَذَا مَعْرُوفٌ فِي كَلَامِ الْعَرَبِ، وَالْمَعْنَى: أَلَّا تَمَسَّهُ النَّارُ أَصْلًا، وَتَمَّ الْكَلَامُ هُنَا، ثُمَّ ابْتُدِئَ: (إِلَّا تَحِلَّةَ الْقَسَمِ)، أَيْ: لَكِنْ تَحِلَّةُ الْقَسَمِ لَا بُدَّ مِنْهَا فِي قَوْلِهِ تَعَالَى: ﴿وَإِنْ مِنْكُمْ إِلَّا وارِدُها﴾، وَهُوَ الْجَوَازُ عَلَى الصِّرَاطِ، أَوِ الرُّؤْيَةُ، أَوِ الدُّخُولُ دُخُولُ سَلَامَةٍ، فَلَا يَكُونُ فِي ذَلِكَ شَيْءٌ مِنْ مَسٍّ، لِقَوْلِهِ عَلَيْهِ الصَّلَاةُ وَالسَّلَامُ: (لَا يَمُوتُ لِأَحَدِكُمْ ثَلَاثَةٌ مِنَ الْوَلَدِ فَيَحْتَسِبُهُمْ إِلَّا كَانُوا لَهُ جُنَّةً مِنَ النَّارِ). وَالْجُنَّةُ: الْوِقَايَةُ وَالسَّتْرُ، وَمَنْ وُقِيَ النَّارَ وَسُتِرَ عَنْهَا فَلَنْ تَمَسَّهُ أَصْلًا، وَلَوْ مَسَّتْهُ لَمَا كَانَ مُوَقًّى.

الرَّابِعَةُ: هَذَا الْحَدِيثُ يُفَسِّرُ الْأَوَّلَ، لِأَنَّ فِيهِ ذِكْرَ الْحِسْبَةِ، وَلِذَلِكَ جَعَلَهُ مَالِكٌ بِأَثَرِهِ مُفَسِّرًا لَهُ. وَيُقَيِّدُ هَذَا الْحَدِيثَ الثَّانِيَ أَيْضًا مَا رَوَاهُ الْبُخَارِيُّ عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ عَنِ النَّبِيِّ (ﷺ): (مَنْ مَاتَ لَهُ ثَلَاثَةٌ مِنَ الْوَلَدِ لَمْ يَبْلُغُوا الْحِنْثَ كَانَ لَهُ حِجَابًا [كَانَ: بِالْإِفْرَادِ، وَاسْمُهَا ضَمِيرٌ يَعُودُ عَلَى الْمَوْتِ الْمَفْهُومِ مِمَّا سَبَقَ، أَيْ: كَانَ مَوْتُهُمْ لَهُ حِجَابًا. وَلِأَبِي ذَرٍّ عَنِ الْكُشْمِيهَنِيِّ: (كَانُوا لَهُ حِجَابًا).

(Qastallani).]] from the Fire, or) entered Paradise. As for his, peace be upon him, saying "they had not reached the age of puberty" (lam yablughu al-hinth) — and its meaning according to the scholars is: they had not reached puberty, and they had not reached the point at which a sin (hinth) would be incumbent upon them — this is evidence that the children of Muslims are in Paradise, and Allah knows best, because when mercy descends upon their fathers it is impossible that they should be shown mercy on account of [whom [[from b, z, t and k.]]] one who is not a recipient of mercy. This is the consensus of the scholars that the children of Muslims are in Paradise. No one has dissented on this except a deviant sect of the Jabriyya, who placed them under the Will of Allah. That view is abandoned and rejected by the consensus of the proofs (al-hujja), whose opposition is not permissible and upon whose like error is not possible; in addition to what has been narrated from the Prophet ﷺ through reliable, trustworthy, upright single-transmitter reports (akhbar al-ahad). And his, peace and blessings be upon him, saying, "The wretched one is he who is wretched in his mother's womb, and the blessed one is he who is blessed in his mother's womb, and that an angel descends and writes his term, his deeds, and his provision," the hadith is specific (makhsus). And whoever of the children of Muslims dies before acquiring (the age of accountability) is among those who were blessed in his mother's womb and was not made wretched, by the evidence of the hadiths and the consensus. Likewise his, peace be upon him, saying to Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her: "O Aisha, Allah created Paradise and created for it its people while they were in the loins of their fathers, and He created the Fire and created for it its people while they were in the loins of their fathers." It is fallen, weak, and rejected by consensus and by the reports; and Talha ibn Yahya, who narrates it, is weak and cannot be relied upon as proof. This hadith is among those transmitted by a single narrator, so it is not to be relied upon. Shu'ba narrated from Mu'awiya ibn Qurra ibn Iyas al-Muzani, from his father, from the Prophet ﷺ that a man from the Ansar had a young son die, and he grieved over him. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him: "Does it not please you that whenever you come to one of the gates of Paradise you find him (the child) waiting to open it for you?" They said: "O Messenger of Allah, is this for him alone, or for the Muslims generally?" He said: "Rather, for the Muslims generally." Abu Umar said: This is a established, sound hadith, in agreement [[in Awb, J, Z, T and K. In Y: i.e.]] with what we have mentioned and with the consensus of the majority, and it contradicts and repels the hadith of Yahya. Abu Umar said: In my view, the correct interpretation of this hadith and similar reports is that they apply to one who maintains the performance of his obligations, avoids major sins, and is patient and seeks reward in his affliction; for the address in that era was directed only to a people the majority of whose condition was as we have described, namely the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them all. Al-Naqqash reported from some of them that he said: The words of Allah, "And there is not one of you but will come to it (waridu-ha)," were abrogated by His words: ﴿Indeed, those for whom the best has preceded from Us — they will be kept far from it﴾ [al-Anbiya: 101]. This is weak, and this is not a place of abrogation (naskh). We have already explained that when the Fire does not touch him, he has been kept far from it. And in a report: "The Fire will say to the believer on the Day of Resurrection: Pass over, O believer, for your light has extinguished my flame."

The fifth issue: the words of Allah the Exalted, ﴿Then it is a decree (kana ʿala rabbika hatman maqḍiyyan)﴾. Al-hatm is the making of a judgment obligatory, meaning that this was a binding decree; "maqḍiyyan" means that Allah decreed it upon you. Ibn Mas'ud said: it means a binding oath.

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Then We shall save those who were mindful of God﴾, that is, We shall deliver them, (and We shall leave the wrongdoers therein on their knees, kneeling). This indicates that "al-warud" means entering, because He did not say "and We shall cause the wrongdoers to enter." This meaning has already been discussed fully. The position is that the perpetrator of a major sin, even if he enters it, will be punished according to the measure of his sin and then he will be saved. The Murji'a said: he will not enter. The Wa'idiyya said: he will remain in it forever. The explanation of this has passed in more than one place. ʿĀṣim al-Jahdari and Mu'awiya ibn Qurra read "thumma nunajji" with a light (sukun-less) form from anjā; this is also the reading of Hamid, Ya'qub and al-Kisa'i. The rest read it with the doubled form. Ibn Abi Layla read "thammah" with a fatha on the tha', meaning "there." "Thumma" is an adverb of place, but it is indeclinable because it is not specific, so it was made indeclinable as "dha" was. The ha' may be for clarifying the vowel, in which case it is dropped in pausal (wasl) recitation, or it may be for feminizing the place, in which case a ta' is retained in connected speech.

The commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on Surah 19, verses 66–72 (part 1 of 3):

The saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And man says, "When I have died, shall I indeed be brought forth alive?"﴾ "Man" here refers to Ubayy ibn Khalaf, who found decayed bones, crumbled them in his hand, and said: "Muhammad claims that we will be resurrected after death." This was reported by al-Kalbi, and mentioned by al-Wahidi, al-Tha'labi and al-Qushayri. Al-Mahdawi said it was revealed concerning al-Walid ibn al-Mughira and his companions, and this is the view of Ibn Abbas. The lam in "la-sawfa ukhraju hayyan" (indeed I shall be brought forth alive) is for emphasis. It is as if he had been told: "When you die, you will indeed be resurrected alive," and so he said: "When I have died, shall I indeed be brought forth alive?" He said this in denial, so the lam appears in the answer as it did in the first statement. Had he been speaking as a new assertion, the lam would not have entered, because it signifies emphasis and affirmation, whereas he was denying the resurrection.

Ibn Dhakwan read "idha ma mittu" as a declarative statement, while the rest read it as an interrogative with the hamza, in accordance with their established readings. Al-Hasan and Abu Haywa read "la-sawfa ukhraju hayyan" as a mocking statement, because they did not believe in the resurrection. Here "man" (al-insan) means the disbeliever.

The saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Does not man remember﴾, that is, does this speaker not remember ("annā khalaqnāhu min qablu") that We created him before, that is, before his question and this statement, ("wa lam yaku shay'an") and he was nothing. Thus re-creation is like the initial creation, so how can he contradict this?

The people of Kufa, except Asim, and the people of Mecca, Abu Amr and Abu Ja'far read "awa-la yadhdhakkaru" (with doubled dhal). Shayba, Nafi' and Asim read "awa-la yadhkuru" (with a single dhal, without doubling). The preferred reading is with the doubling, and its original form is yatadhakkaru, in keeping with the saying of Allah: "Only those of understanding remember" (innama yatadhakkaru ulu al-albab) [See vol. 15, p. 340.] and similar verses. In the codex of Ubayy it is "awa-la yatadhakkaru." This reading is taken as an explanation, because it differs from the script of the Mushaf. The meaning of "yatadhakkaru" is "to reflect," and the meaning of "yadhkuru" is "to become alert and to know," as stated by al-Nahhas.

The saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿So by your Lord, We shall surely gather them﴾: He swore by His own Self, after establishing the proof, that He would gather them from their graves to the Return, just as He gathers the believers.

﴿and the devils﴾, that is, and We shall surely gather the devils as their companions. It has been said: every disbeliever will be gathered with a devil in a chain, as He said: "Gather those who did wrong and their companions" [al-Saffat: 22] (cited by al-Zamakhshari). The "wa" in "wa-al-shayatin" may be conjunctive, or it may mean "with"; and the meaning "with" is more fitting. The meaning is that they will be gathered together with their companions from the devils who misled them, each disbeliever being chained together with a devil. [In one manuscript: "yuqarinu" (they will be paired); in another: "yuhsharu" (will be gathered).] If you ask: this applies if "man" is intended to mean disbelievers specifically; but if it is intended to mean human beings in general, how can their being gathered with the devils be sound? I say: when all people are gathered in a single gathering, and among them are the disbelievers, paired with devils, then they have been gathered with the devils just as they have been gathered with the disbelievers. If you ask: why were the blessed not separated from the wretched at the gathering, as they were separated from them in the recompense? I say: they are not distinguished from one another at the place of assembly, and they are brought to be present where they kneel around Hell, and they are brought to the Fire along with them, so that the blessed may witness the conditions from which Allah saved them and delivered them. Thereby they will increase in joy and gladness upon gladness, and they will gloat over the enemies of Allah and their own enemies, so that the distress and grief of the wretched will increase, along with the vexation that the happiness of the friends of Allah causes them and their gloating over them. If you ask: what is the meaning of bringing them forth on their knees (jithiyyan)? I say: if "man" is understood specifically, the meaning is that they will be driven violently from the place of gathering to the shore of Hell, ("utlan") [Al-'utul: pushing and driving forcefully by violent herding. "Qa'ada mustawfiz": sitting unsettled, not at ease.] in the state they were in at the place of standing, kneeling on their knees, not walking on their feet. This is because the people of the place of standing are described as kneeling. Allah, the Exalted, said: "And you will see every community kneeling" [al-Jathiya: 28]. This is in the customary state of disputes and exchanges, where people kneel upon their knees. This is because of the restlessness and unease it involves, and "al-jatha" means the absence of tranquility; or it is because of the severity of the matter that overwhelms them, so that they cannot stand on their feet and kneel on their knees. If "man" is understood generally, the meaning is that they will kneel when they reach the shore of Hell. And "jithiyyan" is a circumstantial state that is anticipated, since they were in the place of standing kneeling, for that is part of the standing for reckoning, before arriving at reward and punishment.

It is said that the meaning of "We shall surely bring them forth around Hell, kneeling" (jithiyyan) is kneeling on their knees, according to Mujahid and Qatada, meaning that because of the severity of their condition they are unable to stand. "Around Hell" (hawla jahannam) may mean within it, as one says: "The people sat around the house," meaning inside it, surrounding it. So the phrase "around Hell" on this interpretation may be after entering, and it may be before entering.

"Jithiyy" is the plural of "jathin." It is said: "jatha 'ala rukbatayhi, yajthu wa yajthi juthuwwan wa juthiyyan," on the pattern fu'ul in both forms. "Ajthahu ghayruhu" means another made him kneel. A people may be called "juthiyy" as in "jalasa juluusan" (he sat), and the people are "juluus" and "jithiyy," also with a kasra on the jim because of the kasra after it. Ibn Abbas said: "jithiyyan" means in groups. Muqatil said: "jam'an jam'an" (in gatherings). On this interpretation, it is the plural of "juthwa," "jathwa" and "jithwa," three dialectal forms, meaning gathered stones and gathered earth. Thus the people of wine are apart, and the people of fornication are apart. Likewise Tarafa said:

"You see two mounds of earth upon them,
Hard slabs of closely laid stone upon them."

Al-Hasan and al-Dahhak said: "jathiyatan" means kneeling on the knees. On this interpretation it is the plural of "jathin," as explained earlier. This is because of the narrowness of the place, meaning that they cannot sit fully. It was also said: "jithiyyan" means kneeling on their knees for disputing, as in the saying of Allah: "Then on the Day of Resurrection, before your Lord, you will dispute" [al-Zumar: 31] [See vol. 15, p. 254.]. Al-Kumayt said:

"They left their nobles kneeling,
While they, beneath the nobles, were bound together."

The saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Then We shall surely draw out from every sect﴾, that is, We shall extract from every community and every religious group ("ayyuhum ashaddu 'ala al-Rahman 'itiyya") whichever of them is most defiant against the Most Merciful.

Al-Nahhas said: This is a verse difficult in its grammatical analysis (i'rab), because all the readers recite "ayyuhum" with a nominative ending except Harun the Blind reader, for Sibawayh related from him: "Thumma lananzi'anna min kulli shi'atin ayyahum" with the accusative, governed by "lananzi'anna" (we shall surely draw out). Abu Ishaq said: there are three opinions concerning the nominative of "ayyuhum." Al-Khalil ibn Ahmad said, as related from him by Sibawayh, that it is nominative by way of quotation, the meaning being: "Then We shall surely draw out from every sect the one who is said, because of his defiance: which of them is most defiant against the Most Merciful." Al-Khalil recited:

"I have spent nights with a girl in a place,
So I spent the night neither troubled nor deprived."

That is, I spent the night in the position of one of whom it is said: "He is neither troubled nor deprived." Abu Ja'far al-Nahhas said: I saw Abu Ishaq choose this opinion and approve of it. He said: because it is the meaning of the statement of the people of tafsir. He also claimed that the meaning of "Then We shall surely draw out from every sect" is: then We shall surely draw out from every group the most defiant, then the next most defiant. It is as if the torment begins with the most defiant among them, then the one after him. This is the exact wording of Abu Ishaq regarding the meaning of the verse.

Yunus said: "lananzi'anna" has the status of verbs that are cancelled (in their governing), and "ayyuhum" is nominative as the subject. Al-Mahdawi said: the verb is "lananzi'anna," and according to Yunus it is suspended (mu'allaq). Abu Ali said: the meaning of that is that it governs the position of "ayyuhum ashaddu," not that it is cancelled. Al-Khalil and Sibawayh do not suspend a verb like "lananzi'anna" with such a construction; suspension applies only to verbs of doubt and what resembles them, when the occurrence is not certain.

Sibawayh said: "ayyuhum" is built on damma, because it differs from its sisters in the matter of omission. For if you say "ra'aytu alladhi afdalu" (I saw the one who is more excellent) or "man afdalu" (who is more excellent), it is ugly, until you say "man huwa afdalu" (who is he who is more excellent). The omission in "ayyihim" is permissible. Abu Ja'far said: I do not know of any grammarian who has not criticized Sibawayh on this point. I heard Abu Ishaq say: it does not appear clear to me that Sibawayh erred in his book except in two places, and this is one of them. He said: We know that Sibawayh parsed "ayy" as declinable, since it is put in construct, so how can he make it indeclinable when it is in construct? Abu Ishaq did not mention, as far as I know, anything beyond these three opinions. Abu Ali said: the construction on the school of Sibawayh is necessary, because he omitted from it what makes it definite, namely the pronoun, while needing it, just as it is omitted in "min qablu wa min ba'du" [al-Rum: 4] (the two words by which they are defined), in that the attributive clause (silah) clarifies and explains the relative pronoun, just as the second noun in construct clarifies and specifies the first.

Abu Ja'far said: there are four other opinions besides these three mentioned by Abu Ishaq. Al-Kisa'i said: "lananzi'anna" governs the meaning, as one says: "I wore some of the garments and I ate some of the food," and "lananzi'anna" does not govern "ayyuhum" so as to put it in the accusative. Al-Mahdawi added: the verb according to him governs the place of "min kulli shi'atin," and the statement "ayyuhum ashaddu" is a new sentence, nominative as the subject. Sibawayh does not hold that "min" is added in an affirmative sentence. Al-Farra' said: the meaning is "thumma lananzi'anna" by calling (bi-al-nida'), and the meaning of "lananzi'anna" is "lananadiyanna" (we shall surely call out). Al-Mahdawi said: "nada" is a verb that is suspended when followed by a sentence, like "zanantu" (I thought), so it governs in meaning but does not govern in wording. Abu Ja'far said: Abu Bakr ibn Shuqayr related that some of the Kufans say concerning "ayyuhum" that it has the meaning of a condition and conditional consequence, and therefore what precedes it does not govern it. The meaning is: "Then We shall surely draw out from every sect, whether they follow one another or do not follow one another," just as you say: "I struck the people, whichever of them became angry," meaning whether they became angry or did not become angry.

Abu Ja'far said: these are six opinions. I heard Ali ibn Sulayman relate from Muhammad ibn Yazid that he said: "ayyuhum" is connected to "shi'atin" (sect), so it is nominative as the subject, and the meaning is: "Then We shall surely draw out from those who followed one another whichever of them" (ayyuhum), that is, from those who cooperated, so they look at which of them is most defiant against the Most Merciful. This is a good opinion. Al-Kisa'i related that "tashaya'a" means cooperation. "'Itiyyan" is in the accusative as clarification (tamyiz).

The saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Then indeed We are most knowing of those who most deserve to be burned therein﴾ (verse 70). [In the margin: "(Sallyan)" with a damma on the sad is the reading of Nafi', and the exegesis is based on it.] That is, most deserving of entering the Fire. It is said: "salla yasla sulliyyan," like "madha al-shay'u yamdi mudiyyan" (the thing passed away) when it departs, and "hawa yahwi huwiyyan" (he fell) . Al-Jawhari said: it is said: "salayt al-rajul naran" when you make the man enter the Fire and make him burn in it. If you cast him into it with force, as though you intend burning, you say: "asleytuhu" with alif, and "salayatuhu tasliyatan." Those who read it with a light ending say: from the expression: "salya fulan bi-al-nar" (with kasra), "yasla sillyyan," meaning he was burned. Allah, the Exalted, said: "they are most deserving of it, burning" (ṣilyyan). Al-Ajjaj said:

"By Allah, were it not for the Fire that we would burn in it,
Or the people invoking Allah against us,
We would not have heard the obedience of the commander."

[He is ascribed in Lisan al-Arab, under the root (fih), to al-Zafayan, and he cited it in verses which are:
"What is the matter with an eye that wept for its longing,
Over the traces of a dwelling worn by its decay?
By Allah, were it not for the Fire that we would burn in it,
Or the people invoking Allah against us,
We would not have heard the obedience of the commander."
"Alqahu": obedience.]

It is also said: "saliya bi-al-amr" when he endured its heat and severity. Al-Tuhawi said:

[The verse of al-Tuhawi is not completed in the text.]

بَسَالَتُهُمْ وَإِنْ هُمْ ... صَلُوا بِالْحَرْبِ حِينًا بَعْدَ حِينٍ
وَاصْطَلَيْتُ بِالنَّارِ وَتَصَلَّيْتُ بِهَا. قَالَ أَبُو زُبَيْدٍ:
وَقَدْ تَصَلَّيْتُ حَرَّ حَرْبِهِمْ ... كَمَا تَصَلَّى الْمَقْرُورُ مِنْ قَرَسٍ
وَفُلَانٌ لَا يُصْطَلَى بِنَارِهِ إِذَا كَانَ شُجَاعًا لَا يُطَاقُ.

قَوْلُهُ تَعَالَى: ﴿وَإِنْ مِنْكُمْ إِلَّا وارِدُها كانَ عَلى رَبِّكَ حَتْماً مَقْضِيًّا﴾ فِيهِ خَمْسُ مَسَائِلَ:

الْأُولَى: قَوْلُهُ تَعَالَى: ﴿وَإِنْ مِنْكُمْ﴾ هَذَا قَسَمٌ وَالْوَاوُ يَتَضَمَّنُهُ. وَيُفَسِّرُهُ حَدِيثُ النَّبِيِّ (ﷺ): (لَا يَمُوتُ لِأَحَدٍ مِنَ الْمُسْلِمِينَ ثَلَاثَةٌ مِنَ الْوَلَدِ فَتَمَسُّهُ النَّارُ إِلَّا تَحِلَّةَ الْقَسَمِ).
([إِلَّا تَحِلَّةَ الْقَسَمِ]: أَيْ لَا يَدْخُلُ النَّارَ لِيُعَاقَبَ بِهَا، وَلَكِنَّهُ يَجُوزُ عَلَيْهَا، فَلَا يَكُونُ ذَلِكَ إِلَّا بِقَدْرِ مَا يُبِرُّ اللَّهُ بِهِ قَسَمَهُ.)
قَالَ الزُّهْرِيُّ: كَأَنَّهُ يُرِيدُ هَذِهِ الْآيَةَ ﴿وَإِنْ مِنْكُمْ إِلَّا وارِدُها﴾. ذَكَرَهُ أَبُو دَاوُدَ الطَّيَالِسِيُّ. فَقَوْلُهُ: "إِلَّا تَحِلَّةَ الْقَسَمِ" يُخَرَّجُ فِي التَّفْسِيرِ الْمُسْنَدِ، لِأَنَّ الْقَسَمَ الْمَذْكُورَ فِي هَذَا الْحَدِيثِ مَعْنَاهُ عِنْدَ أَهْلِ الْعِلْمِ قَوْلُهُ تَعَالَى: ﴿وَإِنْ مِنْكُمْ إِلَّا وارِدُها﴾. وَقَدْ قِيلَ إِنَّ الْمُرَادَ بِالْقَسَمِ قَوْلُهُ تَعَالَى: ﴿وَالذَّارِياتِ ذَرْواً﴾ إِلَى قَوْلِهِ: ﴿إِنَّما تُوعَدُونَ لَصادِقٌ. وَإِنَّ الدِّينَ لَواقِعٌ﴾ [راجع ج ١٧ ص ٢٩]. وَالْأَوَّلُ أَشْهَرُ، وَالْمَعْنَى مُتَقَارِبٌ.

الثَّانِيَةُ: اخْتَلَفَ النَّاسُ فِي الْوُرُودِ، فَقِيلَ: الْوُرُودُ الدُّخُولُ. رُوِيَ عَنْ جَابِرِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ قَالَ: سَمِعْتُ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ (ﷺ) يَقُولُ: (الْوُرُودُ الدُّخُولُ، لَا يَبْقَى بَرٌّ وَلَا فَاجِرٌ إِلَّا دَخَلَهَا، فَتَكُونُ عَلَى الْمُؤْمِنِينَ بَرْدًا وَسَلَامًا كَمَا كَانَتْ عَلَى إِبْرَاهِيمَ). ﴿ثُمَّ نُنَجِّي الَّذِينَ اتَّقَوْا وَنَذَرُ الظَّالِمِينَ فِيها جِثِيًّا﴾. أَسْنَدَهُ أَبُو عُمَرَ فِي كِتَابِ "التَّمْهِيدِ". وَهُوَ قَوْلُ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ وَخَالِدِ بْنِ مَعْدَانَ وَابْنِ جُرَيْجٍ وَغَيْرِهِمْ.

وَرُوِيَ عَنْ يُونُسَ [عَنِ الْحُسَيْنِ] أَنَّهُ كَانَ يَقْرَأُ: ﴿وَإِنْ مِنْكُمْ إِلَّا وارِدُها﴾ "الْوُرُودُ الدُّخُولُ" عَلَى التَّفْسِيرِ لِلْوُرُودِ، فَغَلِطَ فِيهِ بَعْضُ الرُّوَاةِ فَأَلْحَقَهُ بِالْقُرْآنِ.

وَفِي مُسْنَدِ الدَّارِمِيِّ عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ مَسْعُودٍ قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ (ﷺ): (يَرِدُ النَّاسُ النَّارَ ثُمَّ يَصْدُرُونَ مِنْهَا بِأَعْمَالِهِمْ، فَأَوَّلُهُمْ كَلَمْحِ الْبَرْقِ، ثُمَّ كَالرِّيحِ، ثُمَّ كَحُضْرِ الْفَرَسِ، ثُمَّ كَالرَّاكِبِ الْمُجِدِّ فِي رَحْلِهِ، ثُمَّ كَشَدِّ الرَّجُلِ فِي مِشْيَتِهِ).
[الْحُضْرُ (بِالضَّمِّ): الْعَدْوُ، وَشَدُّ الرَّجُلِ: عَدْوُهُ أَيْضًا.]

وَرُوِيَ عَنِ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ أَنَّهُ قَالَ فِي هَذِهِ الْمَسْأَلَةِ لِنَافِعِ بْنِ الْأَزْرَقِ الْخَارِجِيِّ: أَمَّا أَنَا وَأَنْتَ فَلَا بُدَّ أَنْ نَرِدَهَا؛ أَمَّا أَنَا فَيُنْجِينِي اللَّهُ مِنْهَا، وَأَمَّا أَنْتَ فَمَا أَظُنُّهُ يُنْجِيكَ لِتَكْذِيبِكَ.

وَقَدْ أَشْفَقَ كَثِيرٌ مِنَ الْعُلَمَاءِ مِنْ تَحَقُّقِ الْوُرُودِ وَالْجَهْلِ بِالصَّدْرِ، وَقَدْ بَيَّنَّاهُ فِي "التَّذْكِرَةِ".

وَقَالَتْ فِرْقَةٌ: الْوُرُودُ الْمَمَرُّ عَلَى الصِّرَاطِ. وَرُوِيَ ذَلِكَ عَنِ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ وَابْنِ مَسْعُودٍ وَكَعْبِ الْأَحْبَارِ وَالسُّدِّيِّ، وَرَوَاهُ السُّدِّيُّ عَنِ ابْنِ مَسْعُودٍ عَنِ النَّبِيِّ (ﷺ). وَقَالَهُ الْحَسَنُ أَيْضًا، قَالَ: لَيْسَ الْوُرُودُ الدُّخُولَ، إِنَّمَا تَقُولُ: وَرَدْتُ الْبَصْرَةَ وَلَمْ أَدْخُلْهَا. قَالَ: فَالْوُرُودُ أَنْ يَمُرُّوا عَلَى الصِّرَاطِ.

قَالَ أَبُو بَكْرٍ الْأَنْبَارِيُّ: وَقَدْ بَنَى عَلَى مَذْهَبِ الْحَسَنِ قَوْمٌ مِنْ أَهْلِ اللُّغَةِ، وَاحْتَجُّوا بِقَوْلِ اللَّهِ تَعَالَى: ﴿إِنَّ الَّذِينَ سَبَقَتْ لَهُمْ مِنَّا الْحُسْنى أُولئِكَ عَنْها مُبْعَدُونَ﴾ [راجع ص ٣٤٥ مِنْ هَذَا الْجُزْءِ]. قَالُوا: فَلَا يَدْخُلُ النَّارَ مَنْ ضَمِنَ اللَّهُ أَنْ يُبْعِدَهُ مِنْهَا. وَكَانَ هَؤُلَاءِ يَقْرَءُونَ "ثَمَّ" بِفَتْحِ الثَّاءِ: ﴿ثَمَّ نُنَجِّي الَّذِينَ اتَّقَوْا﴾.

وَاحْتَجَّ عَلَيْهِمُ الْآخَرُونَ، أَهْلُ الْمَقَالَةِ الْأُولَى، بِأَنَّ مَعْنَى قَوْلِهِ: ﴿أُولئِكَ عَنْها مُبْعَدُونَ﴾ عَنِ الْعَذَابِ فِيهَا وَالْإِحْرَاقِ بِهَا. قَالُوا: فَمَنْ دَخَلَهَا وَهُوَ لَا يَشْعُرُ بِهَا وَلَا يُحِسُّ مِنْهَا وَجَعًا وَلَا أَلَمًا، فَهُوَ مُبْعَدٌ عَنْهَا فِي الْحَقِيقَةِ. وَيَسْتَدِلُّونَ بِقَوْلِهِ تَعَالَى: ﴿ثُمَّ نُنَجِّي الَّذِينَ اتَّقَوْا﴾ بِضَمِّ الثَّاءِ، فَ"ثُمَّ" تَدُلُّ عَلَى نَجَاءٍ بَعْدَ الدُّخُولِ.

قُلْتُ: وَفِي صَحِيحِ مُسْلِمٍ: (ثُمَّ يُضْرَبُ الْجِسْرُ عَلَى جَهَنَّمَ، وَتَحِلُّ الشَّفَاعَةُ، فَيَقُولُونَ: اللَّهُمَّ سَلِّمْ سَلِّمْ). قِيلَ: يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ وَمَا الْجِسْرُ؟ قَالَ: (دَحْضٌ مَزِلَّةٌ [دَحْضٌ مَزِلَّةٌ: هُمَا بِمَعْنًى، وَهُوَ الْمَوْضِعُ الَّذِي تَنْزِلُ فِيهِ الْأَقْدَامُ وَلَا تَسْتَقِرُّ] فِيهِ خَطَاطِيفُ وَكَلَالِيبُ وَحَسَكٌ، تَكُونُ بِنَجْدٍ، فِيهَا شُوَيْكَةٌ يُقَالُ لَهَا السَّعْدَانُ، فَيَمُرُّ الْمُؤْمِنُونَ كَطَرْفِ الْعَيْنِ، وَكَالْبَرْقِ، وَكَالرِّيحِ، وَكَالطَّيْرِ، وَكَأَجَاوِيدِ الْخَيْلِ وَالرِّكَابِ، فَنَاجٍ مُسَلَّمٌ، وَمَخْدُوشٌ مُرْسَلٌ، وَمَكْدُوسٌ فِي نَارِ جَهَنَّمَ) الْحَدِيثَ.

وَبِهِ احْتَجَّ مَنْ قَالَ: إِنَّ الْجَوَازَ عَلَى الصِّرَاطِ هُوَ الْوُرُودُ الَّذِي تَضَمَّنَتْهُ هَذِهِ الْآيَةُ، لَا الدُّخُولُ فِيهَا.

وَقَالَتْ فِرْقَةٌ: بَلْ هُوَ وُرُودُ إِشْرَافٍ وَاطِّلَاعٍ وَقُرْبٍ، وَذَلِكَ أَنَّهُمْ يَحْضُرُونَ مَوْضِعَ الْحِسَابِ، وَهُوَ بِقُرْبِ جَهَنَّمَ، فَيَرَوْنَهَا وَيَنْظُرُونَ إِلَيْهَا فِي حَالَةِ الْحِسَابِ، ثُمَّ يُنَجِّي اللَّهُ الَّذِينَ اتَّقَوْا مِمَّا نَظَرُوا إِلَيْهِ وَيُصَارُ بِهِمْ إِلَى الْجَنَّةِ، ﴿وَنَذَرُ الظَّالِمِينَ﴾ أَيْ يُؤْمَرُ بِهِمْ إِلَى النَّارِ. قَالَ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى: ﴿وَلَمَّا وَرَدَ ماءَ مَدْيَنَ﴾ [راجع ج ١٣ ص ٢٦٧] أَيْ أَشْرَفَ عَلَيْهِ، لَا أَنَّهُ دَخَلَهُ. وَقَالَ زُهَيْرٌ:
فَلَمَّا وَرَدْنَ الْمَاءَ زُرْقًا [يُقَالُ: مَاءٌ أَزْرَقُ إِذَا كَانَ صَافِيًا. وَجِمَامُهُ: جَمْعُ جَمٍّ، وَهُوَ الْمَاءُ الْمُجْتَمِعُ. وَالْحَاضِرُ: النَّازِلُ عَلَى الْمَاءِ. وَالْمُتَخَيِّمُ: الْمُقِيمُ، وَأَصْلُهُ مِنْ تَخَيَّمَ إِذَا نَصَبَ الْخَيْمَةَ. يَصِفُ زُهَيْرٌ الظَّعَائِنَ بِأَنَّهُنَّ فِي أَمْنٍ وَمَنَعَةٍ، فَإِذَا نَزَلْنَ نَزَلْنَ آمِنَاتٍ كَنُزُولِ مَنْ هُوَ فِي أَهْلِهِ وَوَطَنِهِ. وَالْبَيْتُ مِنْ مُعَلَّقَتِهِ.]
جِمَامُهُ ... وَضَعْنَ عِصِيَّ الْحَاضِرِ الْمُتَخَيِّمِ

وَرَوَتْ حَفْصَةُ أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ (ﷺ) قَالَ: (لَا يَدْخُلُ النَّارَ أَحَدٌ مِنْ أَهْلِ بَدْرٍ وَالْحُدَيْبِيَةِ). قَالَتْ: فَقُلْتُ: يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ، وَأَيْنَ قَوْلُ اللَّهِ تَعَالَى: ﴿وَإِنْ مِنْكُمْ إِلَّا وارِدُها﴾؟ فَقَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ (ﷺ): (فَمَهْ! ﴿ثُمَّ نُنَجِّي الَّذِينَ اتَّقَوْا وَنَذَرُ الظَّالِمِينَ فِيها جِثِيًّا﴾). أَخْرَجَهُ مُسْلِمٌ مِنْ حَدِيثِ أُمِّ مُبَشِّرٍ، قَالَتْ: سَمِعْتُ النَّبِيَّ (ﷺ) يَقُولُ عِنْدَ حَفْصَةَ الْحَدِيثَ.

وَرَجَّحَ الزَّجَّاجُ هَذَا الْقَوْلَ بِقَوْلِهِ تَعَالَى: ﴿إِنَّ الَّذِينَ سَبَقَتْ لَهُمْ مِنَّا الْحُسْنى أُولئِكَ عَنْها مُبْعَدُونَ﴾.

وَقَالَ مُجَاهِدٌ: وُرُودُ الْمُؤْمِنِينَ النَّارَ هُوَ الْحُمَّى الَّتِي تُصِيبُ الْمُؤْمِنَ فِي دَارِ الدُّنْيَا، وَهِيَ حَظُّ الْمُؤْمِنِ مِنَ النَّارِ، فَلَا يَرِدُهَا. وَرَوَى أَبُو هُرَيْرَةَ أَنَّ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ (ﷺ) عَادَ مَرِيضًا مِنْ وَعْكٍ بِهِ، فَقَالَ لَهُ النَّبِيُّ (ﷺ): (أَبْشِرْ، فَإِنَّ اللَّهَ تَبَارَكَ وَتَعَالَى يَقُولُ: "هِيَ نَارِي أُسَلِّطُهَا عَلَى عَبْدِيَ الْمُؤْمِنِ لِتَكُونَ حَظَّهُ مِنَ النَّارِ").

[أَسْنَدَهُ أَبُو عُمَرَ قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا عَبْدُ الْوَارِثِ بْنُ سُفْيَانَ قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا قَاسِمُ بْنُ أَصْبَغَ قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا مُحَمَّدُ بْنُ إِسْمَاعِيلَ الصَّائِغُ قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا أَبُو أُسَامَةَ قَالَ: حَدَّثَنَا عَبْدُ الرَّحْمَنِ بْنُ يَزِيدَ بْنِ جَابِرٍ عَنْ إِسْمَاعِيلَ بْنِ عُبَيْدِ اللَّهِ [عَنْ أَبِي صَالِحٍ الْأَشْعَرِيِّ] عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ عَنِ النَّبِيِّ (ﷺ) عَادَ مَرِيضًا فَذَكَرَهُ.] [الزِّيَادَةُ مِنْ (تَهْذِيبِ التَّهْذِيبِ) وَتَفْسِيرِ الطَّبَرِيِّ.]

وَفِي الْحَدِيثِ: (الْحُمَّى حَظُّ الْمُؤْمِنِ مِنَ النَّارِ).

وَقَالَتْ فِرْقَةٌ: الْوُرُودُ النَّظَرُ إِلَيْهَا فِي الْقَبْرِ، فَيُنَجَّى مِنْهَا الْفَائِزُ، وَيَصْلَاهَا مَنْ قُدِّرَ عَلَيْهِ دُخُولُهَا، ثُمَّ يَخْرُجُ مِنْهَا بِالشَّفَاعَةِ أَوْ بِغَيْرِهَا مِنْ رَحْمَةِ اللَّهِ تَعَالَى. وَاحْتَجُّوا بِحَدِيثِ ابْنِ عُمَرَ: (إِذَا مَاتَ أَحَدُكُمْ عُرِضَ عَلَيْهِ مَقْعَدُهُ بِالْغَدَاةِ وَالْعَشِيِّ) الْحَدِيثَ.

وَرَوَى وَكِيعٌ عَنْ شُعْبَةَ عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ السَّائِبِ عَنْ رَجُلٍ عَنِ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ أَنَّهُ قَالَ فِي قَوْلِ اللَّهِ تَعَالَى: ﴿وَإِنْ مِنْكُمْ إِلَّا وارِدُها﴾ قَالَ: هَذَا خِطَابٌ لِلْكُفَّارِ. وَرُوِيَ عَنْهُ أَنَّهُ كَانَ يَقْرَأُ: ﴿وَإِنْ مِنْهُمْ﴾ رَدًّا عَلَى الْآيَاتِ الَّتِي قَبْلَهَا فِي الْكُفَّارِ، وَهِيَ قَوْلُهُ: ﴿فَوَ رَبِّكَ لَنَحْشُرَنَّهُمْ وَالشَّياطِينَ ثُمَّ لَنُحْضِرَنَّهُمْ حَوْلَ جَهَنَّمَ جِثِيًّا. ثُمَّ لَنَنْزِعَنَّ مِنْ كُلِّ شِيعَةٍ أَيُّهُمْ أَشَدُّ عَلَى الرَّحْمنِ عِتِيًّا. ثُمَّ لَنَحْنُ أَعْلَمُ بِالَّذِينَ هُمْ أَوْلى بِها صِلِيًّا﴾ [مريم: ٦٨ - ٧٠]. وَ﴿وَإِنْ مِنْهُمْ﴾ [مريم: ٧١]. وَكَذَلِكَ قَرَأَ عِكْرِمَةُ وَجَمَاعَةٌ، وَعَلَيْهَا فَلَا شَغَبَ [كَذَا فِي (ب) وَ(ج) وَ(ك) بِالْمُعْجَمَةِ، وَفِي (ا) وَ(ز) وَ(ط) بِالْمُهْمَلَةِ] فِي هَذِهِ الْقِرَاءَةِ.

وَقَالَتْ فِرْقَةٌ: الْمُرَادُ بِ(مِنْكُمْ) الْكَفَرَةُ، وَالْمَعْنَى: قُلْ لَهُمْ يَا مُحَمَّدُ. وَهَذَا التَّأْوِيلُ أَيْضًا سَهْلُ التَّنَاوُلِ، وَالْكَافُ فِي (مِنْكُمْ) رَاجِعَةٌ إِلَى الْهَاءِ فِي (لَنَحْشُرَنَّهُمْ وَالشَّياطِينَ. ثُمَّ لَنُحْضِرَنَّهُمْ حَوْلَ جَهَنَّمَ جِثِيًّا)، فَلَا يُنْكَرُ رُجُوعُ الْكَافِ إِلَى الْهَاءِ، فَقَدْ عُرِفَ ذَلِكَ فِي قَوْلِهِ عَزَّ وَجَلَّ: ﴿وَسَقاهُمْ رَبُّهُمْ شَراباً طَهُوراً. إِنَّ هَذا كانَ لَكُمْ جَزاءً وَكانَ سَعْيُكُمْ مَشْكُوراً﴾ [الإنسان: ٢١ - ٢٢] [راجع ج ١٩ ص ١٤١ فما بعد]، مَعْنَاهُ: كَانَ لَهُمْ، فَرَجَعَتِ الْكَافُ إِلَى الْهَاءِ.

وَقَالَ الْأَكْثَرُ: الْمُخَاطَبُ الْعَالَمُ كُلُّهُ، وَلَا بُدَّ مِنْ وُرُودِ الْجَمِيعِ، وَعَلَيْهِ نَشَأَ الْخِلَافُ فِي الْوُرُودِ، وَقَدْ بَيَّنَّا أَقْوَالَ الْعُلَمَاءِ فِيهِ. وَظَاهِرُ الْوُرُودِ الدُّخُولُ لِقَوْلِهِ عَلَيْهِ الصَّلَاةُ وَالسَّلَامُ: (فَتَمَسُّهُ النَّارُ)، لِأَنَّ الْمَسَّ حَقِيقَتُهُ فِي اللُّغَةِ الْمُمَاسَّةُ، إِلَّا أَنَّهَا تَكُونُ بَرْدًا وَسَلَامًا عَلَى الْمُؤْمِنِينَ، وَيَنْجُونَ مِنْهَا سَالِمِينَ.

قَالَ خَالِدُ بْنُ مَعْدَانَ: إِذَا دَخَلَ أَهْلُ الْجَنَّةِ الْجَنَّةَ قَالُوا: أَلَمْ يَقُلْ رَبُّنَا: ﴿إِنَّا نَرِدُ النَّارَ﴾؟ فَيُقَالُ: لَقَدْ وَرَدْتُمُوهَا فَأُلْقِيَتْ رَمَادًا.

قُلْتُ: وَهَذَا الْقَوْلُ يَجْمَعُ شَتَاتَ الْأَقْوَالِ، فَإِنَّ مَنْ وَرَدَهَا وَلَمْ تُؤْذِهِ بِلَهَبِهَا وَحَرِّهَا فَقَدْ أُبْعِدَ عَنْهَا وَنُجِّيَ مِنْهَا. نَجَّانَا اللَّهُ تَعَالَى مِنْهَا بِفَضْلِهِ وَكَرَمِهِ، وَجَعَلَنَا مِمَّنْ وَرَدَهَا فَدَخَلَهَا سَالِمًا وَخَرَجَ مِنْهَا غَانِمًا.

فَإِنْ قِيلَ: فَهَلْ يَدْخُلُ الْأَنْبِيَاءُ النَّارَ؟ قُلْنَا: لَا نُطْلِقُ هَذَا، وَلَكِنْ نَقُولُ: إِنَّ الْخَلْقَ جَمِيعًا يَرِدُونَهَا كَمَا دَلَّ عَلَيْهِ حَدِيثُ جَابِرٍ أَوَّلَ الْبَابِ، فَالْعُصَاةُ يَدْخُلُونَهَا بِجَرَائِمِهِمْ، وَالْأَوْلِيَاءُ وَالسُّعَدَاءُ لِشَفَاعَتِهِمْ، فَبَيْنَ الدُّخُولَيْنِ بَوْنٌ.

وَقَالَ ابْنُ الْأَنْبَارِيِّ مُحْتَجًّا لِمُصْحَفِ عُثْمَانَ وَقِرَاءَةِ الْعَامَّةِ: جَائِزٌ فِي اللُّغَةِ أَنْ يُرْجَعَ مِنْ خِطَابِ الْغَيْبَةِ إِلَى لَفْظِ الْمُوَاجَهَةِ بِالْخِطَابِ، كَمَا قَالَ: ﴿وَسَقاهُمْ رَبُّهُمْ شَراباً طَهُوراً. إِنَّ هَذا كانَ لَكُمْ جَزاءً وَكانَ سَعْيُكُمْ مَشْكُوراً﴾، فَأَبْدَلَ الْكَافَ مِنَ الْهَاءِ. وَقَدْ تَقَدَّمَ هَذَا الْمَعْنَى فِي (يُونُسَ) [راجع ج ٨ ص ٣٢٤ فما بعد].

الثَّالِثَةُ: الِاسْتِثْنَاءُ فِي قَوْلِهِ عَلَيْهِ السَّلَامُ: (إِلَّا تَحِلَّةَ الْقَسَمِ) يَحْتَمِلُ أَنْ يَكُونَ اسْتِثْنَاءً مُنْقَطِعًا: لَكِنْ تَحِلَّةُ الْقَسَمِ، وَهَذَا مَعْرُوفٌ فِي كَلَامِ الْعَرَبِ، وَالْمَعْنَى: أَلَّا تَمَسَّهُ النَّارُ أَصْلًا، وَتَمَّ الْكَلَامُ هُنَا، ثُمَّ ابْتُدِئَ: (إِلَّا تَحِلَّةَ الْقَسَمِ)، أَيْ: لَكِنْ تَحِلَّةُ الْقَسَمِ لَا بُدَّ مِنْهَا فِي قَوْلِهِ تَعَالَى: ﴿وَإِنْ مِنْكُمْ إِلَّا وارِدُها﴾، وَهُوَ الْجَوَازُ عَلَى الصِّرَاطِ، أَوِ الرُّؤْيَةُ، أَوِ الدُّخُولُ دُخُولُ سَلَامَةٍ، فَلَا يَكُونُ فِي ذَلِكَ شَيْءٌ مِنْ مَسٍّ، لِقَوْلِهِ عَلَيْهِ الصَّلَاةُ وَالسَّلَامُ: (لَا يَمُوتُ لِأَحَدِكُمْ ثَلَاثَةٌ مِنَ الْوَلَدِ فَيَحْتَسِبُهُمْ إِلَّا كَانُوا لَهُ جُنَّةً مِنَ النَّارِ). وَالْجُنَّةُ: الْوِقَايَةُ وَالسَّتْرُ، وَمَنْ وُقِيَ النَّارَ وَسُتِرَ عَنْهَا فَلَنْ تَمَسَّهُ أَصْلًا، وَلَوْ مَسَّتْهُ لَمَا كَانَ مُوَقًّى.

الرَّابِعَةُ: هَذَا الْحَدِيثُ يُفَسِّرُ الْأَوَّلَ، لِأَنَّ فِيهِ ذِكْرَ الْحِسْبَةِ، وَلِذَلِكَ جَعَلَهُ مَالِكٌ بِأَثَرِهِ مُفَسِّرًا لَهُ. وَيُقَيِّدُ هَذَا الْحَدِيثَ الثَّانِيَ أَيْضًا مَا رَوَاهُ الْبُخَارِيُّ عَنْ أَبِي هُرَيْرَةَ عَنِ النَّبِيِّ (ﷺ): (مَنْ مَاتَ لَهُ ثَلَاثَةٌ مِنَ الْوَلَدِ لَمْ يَبْلُغُوا الْحِنْثَ كَانَ لَهُ حِجَابًا [كَانَ: بِالْإِفْرَادِ، وَاسْمُهَا ضَمِيرٌ يَعُودُ عَلَى الْمَوْتِ الْمَفْهُومِ مِمَّا سَبَقَ، أَيْ: كَانَ مَوْتُهُمْ لَهُ حِجَابًا. وَلِأَبِي ذَرٍّ عَنِ الْكُشْمِيهَنِيِّ: (كَانُوا لَهُ حِجَابًا).

(Qastallani).]] from the Fire, or) entered Paradise. As for his, peace be upon him, saying "they had not reached the age of puberty" (lam yablughu al-hinth) — and its meaning according to the scholars is: they had not reached puberty, and they had not reached the point at which a sin (hinth) would be incumbent upon them — this is evidence that the children of Muslims are in Paradise, and Allah knows best, because when mercy descends upon their fathers it is impossible that they should be shown mercy on account of [whom [[from b, z, t and k.]]] one who is not a recipient of mercy. This is the consensus of the scholars that the children of Muslims are in Paradise. No one has dissented on this except a deviant sect of the Jabriyya, who placed them under the Will of Allah. That view is abandoned and rejected by the consensus of the proofs (al-hujja), whose opposition is not permissible and upon whose like error is not possible; in addition to what has been narrated from the Prophet ﷺ through reliable, trustworthy, upright single-transmitter reports (akhbar al-ahad). And his, peace and blessings be upon him, saying, "The wretched one is he who is wretched in his mother's womb, and the blessed one is he who is blessed in his mother's womb, and that an angel descends and writes his term, his deeds, and his provision," the hadith is specific (makhsus). And whoever of the children of Muslims dies before acquiring (the age of accountability) is among those who were blessed in his mother's womb and was not made wretched, by the evidence of the hadiths and the consensus. Likewise his, peace be upon him, saying to Aisha, may Allah be pleased with her: "O Aisha, Allah created Paradise and created for it its people while they were in the loins of their fathers, and He created the Fire and created for it its people while they were in the loins of their fathers." It is fallen, weak, and rejected by consensus and by the reports; and Talha ibn Yahya, who narrates it, is weak and cannot be relied upon as proof. This hadith is among those transmitted by a single narrator, so it is not to be relied upon. Shu'ba narrated from Mu'awiya ibn Qurra ibn Iyas al-Muzani, from his father, from the Prophet ﷺ that a man from the Ansar had a young son die, and he grieved over him. The Messenger of Allah ﷺ said to him: "Does it not please you that whenever you come to one of the gates of Paradise you find him (the child) waiting to open it for you?" They said: "O Messenger of Allah, is this for him alone, or for the Muslims generally?" He said: "Rather, for the Muslims generally." Abu Umar said: This is a established, sound hadith, in agreement [[in Awb, J, Z, T and K. In Y: i.e.]] with what we have mentioned and with the consensus of the majority, and it contradicts and repels the hadith of Yahya. Abu Umar said: In my view, the correct interpretation of this hadith and similar reports is that they apply to one who maintains the performance of his obligations, avoids major sins, and is patient and seeks reward in his affliction; for the address in that era was directed only to a people the majority of whose condition was as we have described, namely the Companions, may Allah be pleased with them all. Al-Naqqash reported from some of them that he said: The words of Allah, "And there is not one of you but will come to it (waridu-ha)," were abrogated by His words: ﴿Indeed, those for whom the best has preceded from Us — they will be kept far from it﴾ [al-Anbiya: 101]. This is weak, and this is not a place of abrogation (naskh). We have already explained that when the Fire does not touch him, he has been kept far from it. And in a report: "The Fire will say to the believer on the Day of Resurrection: Pass over, O believer, for your light has extinguished my flame."

The fifth issue: the words of Allah the Exalted, ﴿Then it is a decree (kana ʿala rabbika hatman maqḍiyyan)﴾. Al-hatm is the making of a judgment obligatory, meaning that this was a binding decree; "maqḍiyyan" means that Allah decreed it upon you. Ibn Mas'ud said: it means a binding oath.

The words of Allah the Exalted: ﴿Then We shall save those who were mindful of God﴾, that is, We shall deliver them, (and We shall leave the wrongdoers therein on their knees, kneeling). This indicates that "al-warud" means entering, because He did not say "and We shall cause the wrongdoers to enter." This meaning has already been discussed fully. The position is that the perpetrator of a major sin, even if he enters it, will be punished according to the measure of his sin and then he will be saved. The Murji'a said: he will not enter. The Wa'idiyya said: he will remain in it forever. The explanation of this has passed in more than one place. ʿĀṣim al-Jahdari and Mu'awiya ibn Qurra read "thumma nunajji" with a light (sukun-less) form from anjā; this is also the reading of Hamid, Ya'qub and al-Kisa'i. The rest read it with the doubled form. Ibn Abi Layla read "thammah" with a fatha on the tha', meaning "there." "Thumma" is an adverb of place, but it is indeclinable because it is not specific, so it was made indeclinable as "dha" was. The ha' may be for clarifying the vowel, in which case it is dropped in pausal (wasl) recitation, or it may be for feminizing the place, in which case a ta' is retained in connected speech.

The commentary of al-Qurtubi (al-Jami' li-Ahkam al-Quran) on Surah 19, verses 66–72 (part 1 of 3):

The saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿And man says, "When I have died, shall I indeed be brought forth alive?"﴾ "Man" here refers to Ubayy ibn Khalaf, who found decayed bones, crumbled them in his hand, and said: "Muhammad claims that we will be resurrected after death." This was reported by al-Kalbi, and mentioned by al-Wahidi, al-Tha'labi and al-Qushayri. Al-Mahdawi said it was revealed concerning al-Walid ibn al-Mughira and his companions, and this is the view of Ibn Abbas. The lam in "la-sawfa ukhraju hayyan" (indeed I shall be brought forth alive) is for emphasis. It is as if he had been told: "When you die, you will indeed be resurrected alive," and so he said: "When I have died, shall I indeed be brought forth alive?" He said this in denial, so the lam appears in the answer as it did in the first statement. Had he been speaking as a new assertion, the lam would not have entered, because it signifies emphasis and affirmation, whereas he was denying the resurrection.

Ibn Dhakwan read "idha ma mittu" as a declarative statement, while the rest read it as an interrogative with the hamza, in accordance with their established readings. Al-Hasan and Abu Haywa read "la-sawfa ukhraju hayyan" as a mocking statement, because they did not believe in the resurrection. Here "man" (al-insan) means the disbeliever.

The saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Does not man remember﴾, that is, does this speaker not remember ("annā khalaqnāhu min qablu") that We created him before, that is, before his question and this statement, ("wa lam yaku shay'an") and he was nothing. Thus re-creation is like the initial creation, so how can he contradict this?

The people of Kufa, except Asim, and the people of Mecca, Abu Amr and Abu Ja'far read "awa-la yadhdhakkaru" (with doubled dhal). Shayba, Nafi' and Asim read "awa-la yadhkuru" (with a single dhal, without doubling). The preferred reading is with the doubling, and its original form is yatadhakkaru, in keeping with the saying of Allah: "Only those of understanding remember" (innama yatadhakkaru ulu al-albab) [See vol. 15, p. 340.] and similar verses. In the codex of Ubayy it is "awa-la yatadhakkaru." This reading is taken as an explanation, because it differs from the script of the Mushaf. The meaning of "yatadhakkaru" is "to reflect," and the meaning of "yadhkuru" is "to become alert and to know," as stated by al-Nahhas.

The saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿So by your Lord, We shall surely gather them﴾: He swore by His own Self, after establishing the proof, that He would gather them from their graves to the Return, just as He gathers the believers.

﴿and the devils﴾, that is, and We shall surely gather the devils as their companions. It has been said: every disbeliever will be gathered with a devil in a chain, as He said: "Gather those who did wrong and their companions" [al-Saffat: 22] (cited by al-Zamakhshari). The "wa" in "wa-al-shayatin" may be conjunctive, or it may mean "with"; and the meaning "with" is more fitting. The meaning is that they will be gathered together with their companions from the devils who misled them, each disbeliever being chained together with a devil. [In one manuscript: "yuqarinu" (they will be paired); in another: "yuhsharu" (will be gathered).] If you ask: this applies if "man" is intended to mean disbelievers specifically; but if it is intended to mean human beings in general, how can their being gathered with the devils be sound? I say: when all people are gathered in a single gathering, and among them are the disbelievers, paired with devils, then they have been gathered with the devils just as they have been gathered with the disbelievers. If you ask: why were the blessed not separated from the wretched at the gathering, as they were separated from them in the recompense? I say: they are not distinguished from one another at the place of assembly, and they are brought to be present where they kneel around Hell, and they are brought to the Fire along with them, so that the blessed may witness the conditions from which Allah saved them and delivered them. Thereby they will increase in joy and gladness upon gladness, and they will gloat over the enemies of Allah and their own enemies, so that the distress and grief of the wretched will increase, along with the vexation that the happiness of the friends of Allah causes them and their gloating over them. If you ask: what is the meaning of bringing them forth on their knees (jithiyyan)? I say: if "man" is understood specifically, the meaning is that they will be driven violently from the place of gathering to the shore of Hell, ("utlan") [Al-'utul: pushing and driving forcefully by violent herding. "Qa'ada mustawfiz": sitting unsettled, not at ease.] in the state they were in at the place of standing, kneeling on their knees, not walking on their feet. This is because the people of the place of standing are described as kneeling. Allah, the Exalted, said: "And you will see every community kneeling" [al-Jathiya: 28]. This is in the customary state of disputes and exchanges, where people kneel upon their knees. This is because of the restlessness and unease it involves, and "al-jatha" means the absence of tranquility; or it is because of the severity of the matter that overwhelms them, so that they cannot stand on their feet and kneel on their knees. If "man" is understood generally, the meaning is that they will kneel when they reach the shore of Hell. And "jithiyyan" is a circumstantial state that is anticipated, since they were in the place of standing kneeling, for that is part of the standing for reckoning, before arriving at reward and punishment.

It is said that the meaning of "We shall surely bring them forth around Hell, kneeling" (jithiyyan) is kneeling on their knees, according to Mujahid and Qatada, meaning that because of the severity of their condition they are unable to stand. "Around Hell" (hawla jahannam) may mean within it, as one says: "The people sat around the house," meaning inside it, surrounding it. So the phrase "around Hell" on this interpretation may be after entering, and it may be before entering.

"Jithiyy" is the plural of "jathin." It is said: "jatha 'ala rukbatayhi, yajthu wa yajthi juthuwwan wa juthiyyan," on the pattern fu'ul in both forms. "Ajthahu ghayruhu" means another made him kneel. A people may be called "juthiyy" as in "jalasa juluusan" (he sat), and the people are "juluus" and "jithiyy," also with a kasra on the jim because of the kasra after it. Ibn Abbas said: "jithiyyan" means in groups. Muqatil said: "jam'an jam'an" (in gatherings). On this interpretation, it is the plural of "juthwa," "jathwa" and "jithwa," three dialectal forms, meaning gathered stones and gathered earth. Thus the people of wine are apart, and the people of fornication are apart. Likewise Tarafa said:

"You see two mounds of earth upon them,
Hard slabs of closely laid stone upon them."

Al-Hasan and al-Dahhak said: "jathiyatan" means kneeling on the knees. On this interpretation it is the plural of "jathin," as explained earlier. This is because of the narrowness of the place, meaning that they cannot sit fully. It was also said: "jithiyyan" means kneeling on their knees for disputing, as in the saying of Allah: "Then on the Day of Resurrection, before your Lord, you will dispute" [al-Zumar: 31] [See vol. 15, p. 254.]. Al-Kumayt said:

"They left their nobles kneeling,
While they, beneath the nobles, were bound together."

The saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Then We shall surely draw out from every sect﴾, that is, We shall extract from every community and every religious group ("ayyuhum ashaddu 'ala al-Rahman 'itiyya") whichever of them is most defiant against the Most Merciful.

Al-Nahhas said: This is a verse difficult in its grammatical analysis (i'rab), because all the readers recite "ayyuhum" with a nominative ending except Harun the Blind reader, for Sibawayh related from him: "Thumma lananzi'anna min kulli shi'atin ayyahum" with the accusative, governed by "lananzi'anna" (we shall surely draw out). Abu Ishaq said: there are three opinions concerning the nominative of "ayyuhum." Al-Khalil ibn Ahmad said, as related from him by Sibawayh, that it is nominative by way of quotation, the meaning being: "Then We shall surely draw out from every sect the one who is said, because of his defiance: which of them is most defiant against the Most Merciful." Al-Khalil recited:

"I have spent nights with a girl in a place,
So I spent the night neither troubled nor deprived."

That is, I spent the night in the position of one of whom it is said: "He is neither troubled nor deprived." Abu Ja'far al-Nahhas said: I saw Abu Ishaq choose this opinion and approve of it. He said: because it is the meaning of the statement of the people of tafsir. He also claimed that the meaning of "Then We shall surely draw out from every sect" is: then We shall surely draw out from every group the most defiant, then the next most defiant. It is as if the torment begins with the most defiant among them, then the one after him. This is the exact wording of Abu Ishaq regarding the meaning of the verse.

Yunus said: "lananzi'anna" has the status of verbs that are cancelled (in their governing), and "ayyuhum" is nominative as the subject. Al-Mahdawi said: the verb is "lananzi'anna," and according to Yunus it is suspended (mu'allaq). Abu Ali said: the meaning of that is that it governs the position of "ayyuhum ashaddu," not that it is cancelled. Al-Khalil and Sibawayh do not suspend a verb like "lananzi'anna" with such a construction; suspension applies only to verbs of doubt and what resembles them, when the occurrence is not certain.

Sibawayh said: "ayyuhum" is built on damma, because it differs from its sisters in the matter of omission. For if you say "ra'aytu alladhi afdalu" (I saw the one who is more excellent) or "man afdalu" (who is more excellent), it is ugly, until you say "man huwa afdalu" (who is he who is more excellent). The omission in "ayyihim" is permissible. Abu Ja'far said: I do not know of any grammarian who has not criticized Sibawayh on this point. I heard Abu Ishaq say: it does not appear clear to me that Sibawayh erred in his book except in two places, and this is one of them. He said: We know that Sibawayh parsed "ayy" as declinable, since it is put in construct, so how can he make it indeclinable when it is in construct? Abu Ishaq did not mention, as far as I know, anything beyond these three opinions. Abu Ali said: the construction on the school of Sibawayh is necessary, because he omitted from it what makes it definite, namely the pronoun, while needing it, just as it is omitted in "min qablu wa min ba'du" [al-Rum: 4] (the two words by which they are defined), in that the attributive clause (silah) clarifies and explains the relative pronoun, just as the second noun in construct clarifies and specifies the first.

Abu Ja'far said: there are four other opinions besides these three mentioned by Abu Ishaq. Al-Kisa'i said: "lananzi'anna" governs the meaning, as one says: "I wore some of the garments and I ate some of the food," and "lananzi'anna" does not govern "ayyuhum" so as to put it in the accusative. Al-Mahdawi added: the verb according to him governs the place of "min kulli shi'atin," and the statement "ayyuhum ashaddu" is a new sentence, nominative as the subject. Sibawayh does not hold that "min" is added in an affirmative sentence. Al-Farra' said: the meaning is "thumma lananzi'anna" by calling (bi-al-nida'), and the meaning of "lananzi'anna" is "lananadiyanna" (we shall surely call out). Al-Mahdawi said: "nada" is a verb that is suspended when followed by a sentence, like "zanantu" (I thought), so it governs in meaning but does not govern in wording. Abu Ja'far said: Abu Bakr ibn Shuqayr related that some of the Kufans say concerning "ayyuhum" that it has the meaning of a condition and conditional consequence, and therefore what precedes it does not govern it. The meaning is: "Then We shall surely draw out from every sect, whether they follow one another or do not follow one another," just as you say: "I struck the people, whichever of them became angry," meaning whether they became angry or did not become angry.

Abu Ja'far said: these are six opinions. I heard Ali ibn Sulayman relate from Muhammad ibn Yazid that he said: "ayyuhum" is connected to "shi'atin" (sect), so it is nominative as the subject, and the meaning is: "Then We shall surely draw out from those who followed one another whichever of them" (ayyuhum), that is, from those who cooperated, so they look at which of them is most defiant against the Most Merciful. This is a good opinion. Al-Kisa'i related that "tashaya'a" means cooperation. "'Itiyyan" is in the accusative as clarification (tamyiz).

The saying of Allah, the Exalted: ﴿Then indeed We are most knowing of those who most deserve to be burned therein﴾ (verse 70). [In the margin: "(Sallyan)" with a damma on the sad is the reading of Nafi', and the exegesis is based on it.] That is, most deserving of entering the Fire. It is said: "salla yasla sulliyyan," like "madha al-shay'u yamdi mudiyyan" (the thing passed away) when it departs, and "hawa yahwi huwiyyan" (he fell) . Al-Jawhari said: it is said: "salayt al-rajul naran" when you make the man enter the Fire and make him burn in it. If you cast him into it with force, as though you intend burning, you say: "asleytuhu" with alif, and "salayatuhu tasliyatan." Those who read it with a light ending say: from the expression: "salya fulan bi-al-nar" (with kasra), "yasla sillyyan," meaning he was burned. Allah, the Exalted, said: "they are most deserving of it, burning" (ṣilyyan). Al-Ajjaj said:

"By Allah, were it not for the Fire that we would burn in it,
Or the people invoking Allah against us,
We would not have heard the obedience of the commander."

[He is ascribed in Lisan al-Arab, under the root (fih), to al-Zafayan, and he cited it in verses which are:
"What is the matter with an eye that wept for its longing,
Over the traces of a dwelling worn by its decay?
By Allah, were it not for the Fire that we would burn in it,
Or the people invoking Allah against us,
We would not have heard the obedience of the commander."
"Alqahu": obedience.]

It is also said: "saliya bi-al-amr" when he endured its heat and severity. Al-Tuhawi said:

[The verse of al-Tuhawi is not completed in the text.]

بَسَالَتُهُمْ وَإِنْ هُمْ ... صَلُوا بِالْحَرْبِ حِينًا بَعْدَ حِينٍ
وَاصْطَلَيْتُ بِالنَّارِ وَتَصَلَّيْتُ بِهَا. قَالَ أَبُو زُبَيْدٍ:
وَقَدْ تَصَلَّيْتُ حَرَّ حَرْبِهِمْ ... كَمَا تَصَلَّى الْمَقْرُورُ مِنْ قَرَسٍ
وَفُلَانٌ لَا يُصْطَلَى بِنَارِهِ إِذَا كَانَ شُجَاعًا لَا يُطَاقُ.

قَوْلُهُ تَعَالَى: ﴿وَإِنْ مِنْكُمْ إِلَّا وارِدُها كانَ عَلى رَبِّكَ حَتْماً مَقْضِيًّا﴾ فِيهِ خَمْسُ مَسَائِلَ:

الْأُولَى: قَوْلُهُ تَعَالَى: ﴿وَإِنْ مِنْكُمْ﴾ هَذَا قَسَمٌ وَالْوَاوُ يَتَضَمَّنُهُ. وَيُفَسِّرُهُ حَدِيثُ النَّبِيِّ (ﷺ): (لَا يَمُوتُ لِأَحَدٍ مِنَ الْمُسْلِمِينَ ثَلَاثَةٌ مِنَ الْوَلَدِ فَتَمَسُّهُ النَّارُ إِلَّا تَحِلَّةَ الْقَسَمِ).
([إِلَّا تَحِلَّةَ الْقَسَمِ]: أَيْ لَا يَدْخُلُ النَّارَ لِيُعَاقَبَ بِهَا، وَلَكِنَّهُ يَجُوزُ عَلَيْهَا، فَلَا يَكُونُ ذَلِكَ إِلَّا بِقَدْرِ مَا يُبِرُّ اللَّهُ بِهِ قَسَمَهُ.)
قَالَ الزُّهْرِيُّ: كَأَنَّهُ يُرِيدُ هَذِهِ الْآيَةَ ﴿وَإِنْ مِنْكُمْ إِلَّا وارِدُها﴾. ذَكَرَهُ أَبُو دَاوُدَ الطَّيَالِسِيُّ. فَقَوْلُهُ: "إِلَّا تَحِلَّةَ الْقَسَمِ" يُخَرَّجُ فِي التَّفْسِيرِ الْمُسْنَدِ، لِأَنَّ الْقَسَمَ الْمَذْكُورَ فِي هَذَا الْحَدِيثِ مَعْنَاهُ عِنْدَ أَهْلِ الْعِلْمِ قَوْلُهُ تَعَالَى: ﴿وَإِنْ مِنْكُمْ إِلَّا وارِدُها﴾. وَقَدْ قِيلَ إِنَّ الْمُرَادَ بِالْقَسَمِ قَوْلُهُ تَعَالَى: ﴿وَالذَّارِياتِ ذَرْواً﴾ إِلَى قَوْلِهِ: ﴿إِنَّما تُوعَدُونَ لَصادِقٌ. وَإِنَّ الدِّينَ لَواقِعٌ﴾ [راجع ج ١٧ ص ٢٩]. وَالْأَوَّلُ أَشْهَرُ، وَالْمَعْنَى مُتَقَارِبٌ.

الثَّانِيَةُ: اخْتَلَفَ النَّاسُ فِي الْوُرُودِ، فَقِيلَ: الْوُرُودُ الدُّخُولُ. رُوِيَ عَنْ جَابِرِ بْنِ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ قَالَ: سَمِعْتُ رَسُولَ اللَّهِ (ﷺ) يَقُولُ: (الْوُرُودُ الدُّخُولُ، لَا يَبْقَى بَرٌّ وَلَا فَاجِرٌ إِلَّا دَخَلَهَا، فَتَكُونُ عَلَى الْمُؤْمِنِينَ بَرْدًا وَسَلَامًا كَمَا كَانَتْ عَلَى إِبْرَاهِيمَ). ﴿ثُمَّ نُنَجِّي الَّذِينَ اتَّقَوْا وَنَذَرُ الظَّالِمِينَ فِيها جِثِيًّا﴾. أَسْنَدَهُ أَبُو عُمَرَ فِي كِتَابِ "التَّمْهِيدِ". وَهُوَ قَوْلُ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ وَخَالِدِ بْنِ مَعْدَانَ وَابْنِ جُرَيْجٍ وَغَيْرِهِمْ.

وَرُوِيَ عَنْ يُونُسَ [عَنِ الْحُسَيْنِ] أَنَّهُ كَانَ يَقْرَأُ: ﴿وَإِنْ مِنْكُمْ إِلَّا وارِدُها﴾ "الْوُرُودُ الدُّخُولُ" عَلَى التَّفْسِيرِ لِلْوُرُودِ، فَغَلِطَ فِيهِ بَعْضُ الرُّوَاةِ فَأَلْحَقَهُ بِالْقُرْآنِ.

وَفِي مُسْنَدِ الدَّارِمِيِّ عَنْ عَبْدِ اللَّهِ بْنِ مَسْعُودٍ قَالَ: قَالَ رَسُولُ اللَّهِ (ﷺ): (يَرِدُ النَّاسُ النَّارَ ثُمَّ يَصْدُرُونَ مِنْهَا بِأَعْمَالِهِمْ، فَأَوَّلُهُمْ كَلَمْحِ الْبَرْقِ، ثُمَّ كَالرِّيحِ، ثُمَّ كَحُضْرِ الْفَرَسِ، ثُمَّ كَالرَّاكِبِ الْمُجِدِّ فِي رَحْلِهِ، ثُمَّ كَشَدِّ الرَّجُلِ فِي مِشْيَتِهِ).
[الْحُضْرُ (بِالضَّمِّ): الْعَدْوُ، وَشَدُّ الرَّجُلِ: عَدْوُهُ أَيْضًا.]

وَرُوِيَ عَنِ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ أَنَّهُ قَالَ فِي هَذِهِ الْمَسْأَلَةِ لِنَافِعِ بْنِ الْأَزْرَقِ الْخَارِجِيِّ: أَمَّا أَنَا وَأَنْتَ فَلَا بُدَّ أَنْ نَرِدَهَا؛ أَمَّا أَنَا فَيُنْجِينِي اللَّهُ مِنْهَا، وَأَمَّا أَنْتَ فَمَا أَظُنُّهُ يُنْجِيكَ لِتَكْذِيبِكَ.

وَقَدْ أَشْفَقَ كَثِيرٌ مِنَ الْعُلَمَاءِ مِنْ تَحَقُّقِ الْوُرُودِ وَالْجَهْلِ بِالصَّدْرِ، وَقَدْ بَيَّنَّاهُ فِي "التَّذْكِرَةِ".

وَقَالَتْ فِرْقَةٌ: الْوُرُودُ الْمَمَرُّ عَلَى الصِّرَاطِ. وَرُوِيَ ذَلِكَ عَنِ ابْنِ عَبَّاسٍ وَابْنِ مَسْعُودٍ وَكَعْبِ الْأَحْبَارِ وَالسُّدِّيِّ، وَرَوَاهُ السُّدِّيُّ عَنِ ابْنِ مَسْعُودٍ عَنِ النَّبِيِّ (ﷺ). وَقَالَهُ الْحَسَنُ أَيْضًا، قَالَ: لَيْسَ الْوُرُودُ الدُّخُولَ، إِنَّمَا تَقُولُ: وَرَدْتُ الْبَصْرَةَ وَلَمْ أَدْخُلْهَا. قَالَ: فَالْوُرُودُ أَنْ يَمُرُّوا عَلَى الصِّرَاطِ.

قَالَ أَبُو بَكْرٍ الْأَنْبَارِيُّ: وَقَدْ بَنَى عَلَى مَذْهَبِ الْحَسَنِ قَوْمٌ مِنْ أَهْلِ اللُّغَةِ، وَاحْتَجُّوا بِقَوْلِ اللَّهِ تَعَالَى: ﴿إِنَّ الَّذِينَ سَبَقَتْ لَهُمْ مِنَّا الْحُسْنى أُولئِكَ عَنْها مُبْعَدُونَ﴾ [راجع ص ٣٤٥ مِنْ هَذَا الْجُزْءِ]. قَالُوا: فَلَا يَدْخُلُ النَّارَ مَنْ ضَمِنَ اللَّهُ أَنْ يُبْعِدَهُ مِنْهَا. وَكَانَ هَؤُلَاءِ يَقْرَءُونَ "ثَمَّ" بِفَتْحِ الثَّاءِ: ﴿ثَمَّ نُنَجِّي الَّذِينَ اتَّقَوْا﴾.

وَاحْتَجَّ عَلَيْهِمُ الْآخَرُونَ، أَهْلُ الْمَقَالَةِ الْأُولَى، بِأَنَّ مَعْنَى قَوْلِهِ: ﴿أُولئِكَ عَنْها مُبْعَدُونَ﴾ عَنِ الْعَذَابِ فِيهَا وَالْإِحْرَاقِ بِهَا. قَالُوا: فَمَنْ دَخَلَهَا وَهُوَ لَا يَشْعُرُ بِهَا وَلَا يُحِسُّ مِنْهَا وَجَعًا وَلَا أَلَمًا، فَهُوَ مُبْعَدٌ عَنْهَا فِي الْحَقِيقَةِ. وَيَسْتَدِلُّونَ بِقَوْلِهِ تَعَالَى: ﴿ثُمَّ نُنَجِّي الَّذِينَ اتَّقَوْا﴾ بِضَمِّ الثَّاءِ، فَ"ثُمَّ" تَدُلُّ عَلَى نَجَاءٍ بَعْدَ الدُّخُولِ.

قُلْتُ: وَفِي صَحِيحِ مُسْلِمٍ: (ثُمَّ يُضْرَبُ الْجِسْرُ عَلَى جَهَنَّمَ، وَتَحِلُّ الشَّفَاعَةُ، فَيَقُولُونَ: اللَّهُمَّ سَلِّمْ سَلِّمْ). قِيلَ: يَا رَسُولَ اللَّهِ وَمَا الْجِسْرُ؟ قَالَ: (دَحْضٌ مَزِلَّةٌ [دَحْضٌ مَزِلَّةٌ: هُمَا بِمَعْنًى، وَهُوَ الْمَوْضِعُ الَّذِي تَنْزِلُ فِيهِ الْأَقْدَامُ وَلَا تَسْتَقِرُّ] فِيهِ خَطَاطِيفُ وَكَلَالِيبُ وَحَسَكٌ، تَكُونُ بِنَجْدٍ، فِيهَا شُوَيْكَةٌ يُقَالُ لَهَا السَّعْدَانُ، فَيَمُرُّ الْمُؤْمِنُونَ كَطَرْفِ الْعَيْنِ، وَكَالْبَرْقِ، وَكَالرِّيحِ، وَكَالطَّيْرِ، وَكَأَجَاوِيدِ الْخَيْلِ وَالرِّكَابِ، فَنَاجٍ مُسَلَّمٌ، وَمَخْدُوشٌ مُرْسَلٌ، وَمَكْدُوسٌ فِي نَارِ جَهَنَّمَ) الْحَدِيثَ.

وَبِهِ احْتَجَّ مَنْ قَالَ: إِنَّ الْجَوَازَ عَلَى الصِّرَاطِ هُوَ الْوُرُودُ الَّذِي تَضَمَّنَتْهُ هَذِهِ الْآيَةُ، لَا الدُّخُولُ فِيهَا.

وَقَالَتْ فِرْقَةٌ: بَلْ هُوَ وُرُودُ إِشْرَافٍ وَاطِّلَاعٍ وَقُرْبٍ، وَذَلِكَ أَنَّهُمْ يَحْضُرُونَ مَوْضِعَ الْحِسَابِ، وَهُوَ بِقُرْبِ جَهَنَّمَ، فَيَرَوْنَهَا وَيَنْظُرُونَ إِلَيْهَا فِي حَالَةِ الْحِسَابِ، ثُمَّ يُنَجِّي اللَّهُ الَّذِينَ اتَّقَوْا مِمَّا نَظَرُوا إِلَيْهِ وَيُصَارُ بِهِمْ إِلَى الْجَنَّةِ، ﴿وَنَذَرُ الظَّالِمِينَ﴾ أَيْ يُؤْمَرُ بِهِمْ إِلَى النَّارِ. قَالَ اللَّهُ تَعَالَى: ﴿وَلَمَّا وَرَدَ ماءَ مَدْيَنَ﴾ [راجع ج ١٣ ص ٢٦٧] أَيْ أَشْرَفَ عَلَيْهِ، لَا أَنَّهُ دَخَلَهُ. وَقَالَ زُهَيْرٌ:
فَلَمَّا وَرَدْنَ الْمَاءَ زُرْقًا [يُقَالُ: مَاءٌ أَزْرَقُ إِذَا كَانَ صَافِيًا. وَجِمَامُهُ: جَمْعُ جَمٍّ، وَهُوَ الْمَاءُ الْمُجْتَمِعُ. وَالْحَاضِرُ: النَّازِلُ عَلَى الْمَاءِ. وَالْمُتَخَيِّمُ: الْمُقِيمُ، وَأَصْلُهُ مِنْ تَخَيَّمَ إِذَا نَصَبَ الْخَيْمَةَ. يَصِفُ زُهَيْرٌ الظَّعَائِنَ بِأَنَّهُنَّ فِي أَمْنٍ وَمَنَعَةٍ، فَإِذَا نَزَلْنَ نَزَلْنَ آمِنَاتٍ كَنُزُولِ مَنْ هُوَ فِي أَهْلِهِ وَوَطَنِهِ. وَالْبَيْتُ مِنْ مُعَلَّقَتِهِ.]
جِمَامُهُ ... وَضَعْنَ عِصِيَّ الْحَاضِرِ الْمُتَخَيِّمِ
